title: Backup Pass 3 (managed identities) is not session-latched and swallows per-MI read failures without recording them in `skipped`
evidence:
backup.rs:675-683 `async fn backup_managed_identities(
    client: &GraphClient,
    managed: &[ServicePrincipal],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    app_handle: &AppHandle,
    done: &Mutex<usize>,
    total: usize,
    throttle: &ConcurrencyThrottle,
) -> Result<Vec<ManagedIdentityBackup>, UiError> {` (no `session: &SessionDead`)
backup.rs:695-706 `.batch_list_app_role_assignments(&mi_ids).await
            // Per-item errors degrade to empty here (best-effort, as before);
            // only a WHOLE-batch failure takes the per-item path.
            .map(|v| v.into_iter().map(Result::unwrap_or_default).collect()),
        |id: String| async move { client.list_app_role_assignments(&id).await.unwrap_or_default() },`
Contrast backup.rs:388-391 (Pass 1) `// A DR backup that silently drops apps is the most dangerous artifact this app produces ... Classify every per-item failure so a dead session aborts the run instead of thinning it.
    note_graph_failures(session, app_jsons.iter().map(Result::as_ref));`
backup.rs:211-216 after Pass 2: `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err("the tenant backup")); }` — no equivalent after Pass 3.
rationale: Passes 1 and 2 were hardened so a dead session aborts the backup and any dropped object lands in `TenantBackup.skipped`. Pass 3 predates that: if the refresh token dies (or Graph 5xx/429s past the retry budget) during the MI phase, every assignment read fails, is replaced with an empty `Vec`, and the run returns `Ok` — a manifest whose managed identities all have `held_app_roles: []`. Restore then re-binds nothing and reports success. The manifest neither records the gap in `skipped` nor fails, which is exactly the 'reads as complete' hazard the module documents for the other passes.
proposal: Thread `session: &SessionDead` into `backup_managed_identities`; keep the per-item `Result` from `batch_or_serial`, call `note_graph_failures(session, ...)` on it, and for each `Err` push `SkippedObject::new("managedIdentity", &sp.id, Some(sp.display_name.clone()), format!("held app-roles could not be read: {err}"))` while still emitting the MI with empty roles (so the operator knows the entry is partial). After the pass, mirror passes 1-2: `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err("the tenant backup")); }`. Return `(Vec<ManagedIdentityBackup>, Vec<SkippedObject>)` and append to `skipped`. Extend the existing wiremock degrade test with a 500 on `/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignments` asserting the skip is recorded. Effort S.

Strong corroboration the reviewer missed: `SkippedObject.kind` is documented as 'application, enterpriseApp, or managedIdentity' (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/backup.rs:78) but backup.rs only ever emits 'application' (:407/:417/:427) and 'enterpriseApp' (:573) — no code path records an MI skip. The in-code comment 'best-effort, as before' is legacy preservation, not a rationale, and docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:113-116 describes Pass 3 without mentioning the degrade. A dead session or exhausted retry budget during Pass 3 yields an Ok manifest whose MIs all carry `held_app_roles: []`, which restore then treats as nothing to re-bind — the 'reads as complete' hazard the module's own doc (dto/backup.rs:59-66) names. High is fair given passes 1-2 were hardened for exactly this and `note_graph_failures` (:346-353) already exists to reuse.
recheck_notes: Failing path constructed end to end. `backup_managed_identities` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/backup.rs:675-683) has no `session: &SessionDead` parameter, and `backup_tenant` calls it at :224-232 then immediately returns `Ok(TenantBackup { ... skipped })` at :234-243 with no `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err(..)) }` — unlike the checks after Pass 1 (:169-171) and Pass 2 (:211-213). Trigger: a refresh-token death (or 429 past `core::http_retry` budget / 5xx) once Pass 3 begins. The token adapter surfaces as `GraphError::Token(TokenError)` (core/http_error.rs:95) whose `ui_code()` passes `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` through (`http_error.rs:131-133` via `reauth::passthrough_code`) — exactly the code `SessionDead::note_code` (dispatch.rs:62-64) would latch, had it been called. `batch_get_json` (graph/src/client/batch.rs:145 `chunk?`) returns whole-batch Err, `batch_or_serial` (dispatch.rs:134-160) falls to per-item `list_app_role_assignments` (graph/src/client/roles_grants.rs:36-40) which fails identically, and every MI ends with `held_app_roles: []` in an `Ok` manifest. Nothing pins this: tests/repo_invariants/fanout.rs:203-221 inspects only `dispatch_capped(` call sites, and Pass 3 deliberately uses the batch helpers' internal concurrency (backup.rs:669-672), so the rule never sees it; grep of repo_invariants/ for `batch_or_serial`, `note_graph_failures`, `backup_managed_identities` finds nothing. Downstream: `restore_managed_identities` (commands/restore.rs:769-793) iterates `mi.held_app_roles`, so an empty list yields `app_roles_rebound: 0` with zero warnings and only the unconditional Azure-RBAC `ManualItem` (:796-803) — the restore reads as a clean success. The `skipped` contract (dto/backup.rs:59-71: "A DR backup that silently drops what it could not read is the most dangerous artifact this app produces ... Restore surfaces the same list") and the DR view that renders it (web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:299-339) confirm this is the intended surfacing mechanism and that Pass 3 bypasses it. The existing wiremock test (backup.rs:1000-1127) covers only `backup_app_chunk`. Note the module comment at :693-694 ('best-effort, as before') documents the degrade, but the architecture doc (docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:113-116 and :101-103) claims 'a per-object failure skips just that object' and passes 1-2 were hardened after that comment was written, so this is a real inconsistency rather than a deliberate exemption. Severity high is warranted: a DR manifest that reads complete but restores no MI permissions is the hazard the module itself ranks as its worst.

title: resolve_mail_scopes hardcodes Microsoft Graph, so the EWS full_access_as_app scope never gets a verdict (Permissions tab shows Unknown forever; audit scores a correctly scoped EWS app org-wide)
rationale: graph_mail_role("full_access_as_app") is None, so the value is dropped in all three resolver paths. get_mail_permission_scopes emits no MailScopeEntry for it (an app declaring only the EWS scope gets an empty Vec cached without any Exchange call); get_mail_scopes_for_principal returns Unknown for it (scopes.get(&value) misses). The audit's lean resolver drops it too, so after a successful `Application EWS.AccessAsApp` scoping the audit still scores the app at org-wide weight (empty map = org-wide). The mod.rs comment justifying MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID is contradicted by the crate's own resource-aware mapping and by the repo's tests; this is not a documented decision but a regression left behind when the value-only helper was deleted.
proposal: Change resolve_mail_scopes and resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached to accept the role alongside the value — e.g. `&[(String, &'static str)]` (the shape get_mail_scopes_for_principal already builds at 377-383) or `&[ExchangeTarget]` (which carries exchange_role) — and stop re-deriving the role inside. Fix the entries filter at 341 to read the role from the target rather than calling exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, ..). Update the audit caller (audit.rs:1553) to pass perms.app_role_grants' (resource, value) pairs. Correct the mod.rs:32-35 comment. Add a unit test that resolve_mail_scopes' output keys include full_access_as_app mapped to "Application EWS.AccessAsApp" and that an EWS-only input does not short-circuit before the probe. Expected effect: the EWS row shows Org-wide/Scoped like Graph rows, and the audit's reduced scoped-mail weight applies to an RBAC-scoped EWS grant.
verifier_notes: Premise holds at every cited line. mail_scopes.rs:108-116, :242 and :341 all call exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, ..); core scoping.rs:106-116 maps full_access_as_app ONLY under OFFICE365_EXCHANGE_ONLINE_APP_ID and graph_mail_role (scoping.rs:77-93) has no EWS arm, so the value is dropped in all three resolver paths. Downstream: get_mail_permission_scopes builds `scopable` from targets_from_declared (mail_scopes.rs:312-315), which exchange/tests.rs:81-106 proves includes full_access_as_app; an EWS-only app therefore passes the empty check at :316, pays exchange_client_checked (consent prompt) at :334, gets an empty map back from resolve_mail_scopes (:114-115), and the :341 filter drops the row, caching an empty Vec (:353). get_mail_scopes_for_principal gates correctly by resource (:377-383) but then feeds bare values into resolve_mail_scopes, so scopes.get misses and the row is Unknown (:432-435). Frontend scope_badge.rs:104-112 renders ScopeCell::Mailbox(Unknown) for (EXO, full_access_as_app) since is_exchange_scopable_on is a re-export of is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission (scope_badge.rs:35), and :330-340 expects a verdict cell for that row. Audit: core audit/types.rs:386-396 scope_mechanism passes the resource gate for (EXO, full_access_as_app) then misses mail_scopes.get → None → full weight; derive_orgwide_mail_scopes (audit.rs:1100-1130) only feeds the reconciliation set, and apply_legacy_policy_verdict (verdict.rs:192-210) only covers the legacy-AAP verdict, never an RBAC 'Application EWS.AccessAsApp' scope. The mod.rs:32-35 rationale ('only Microsoft Graph's mail permissions ever are') is contradicted by scoping.rs:112-114, tests.rs:104 and mail_scopes.rs:422-425 in the same file. No repo_invariants test, doc (exchange-scoping.md:98-140 describes the EWS row as scopable and rendered) or CHANGELOG entry documents Graph-only resolution as deliberate. One caveat: the 'regression when the value-only helper was deleted' history claim is unverifiable — the repo history is squashed at 0389543 (exchange.rs lands whole, 2987 insertions) — but that does not affect the code-level verdict. Proposal (pass (value, role) or ExchangeTarget, fix :341, correct mod.rs comment, add a unit test) is feasible and consistent with the 'carry the resource, never the bare value' rule.

Could not refute; every path traced end to end reproduces the defect in the shipped build.

(3) Held path (enterprise app / MI pane): get_mail_scopes_for_principal's gate at :377-383 is resource-aware and keeps the EWS pair, but :426-427 passes values only into resolve_mail_scopes, which drops it; :432-435 falls back to MailPermissionScope::Unknown for that entry and caches it (:443).

(4) Audit: audit.rs:1260 pushes ResourcePermission::exchange_online(EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP) into app_role_grants, so `declared_values = perms.app_role_values()` (audit.rs:1523; core/audit/types.rs:338-343) includes it; resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached filters it away at mail_scopes.rs:240-244 (and excludes it from the cache key). core/audit/types.rs:386-397 scope_mechanism reads mail_scopes.get(&grant.value) -> None -> full org-wide weight for an app whose only mailbox grant is an RBAC-scoped `Application EWS.AccessAsApp`. Only apply_legacy_policy_verdict (audit.rs:1585) can ever mark the EWS grant scoped, and only via a surviving legacy AAP, not RBAC.

(5) Not a documented decision: docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:31-33 says the probe/badge paths were meant to use the value-only role form precisely because "the two resources share no mapped value names" (i.e. EWS is unambiguous there). The value-only form was then deleted and pinned out by repo_invariants/commands.rs:129-134, and the replacement at mail_scopes.rs:101-107 / mod.rs:32-35 asserts "only Microsoft Graph's mail permissions ever are" scopable, which scoping.rs:113 and the deep-dive contradict. No unit test or repo invariant covers resolve_mail_scopes' output for the EWS value (the only resolver test, exchange/tests.rs:200-231, uses a non-mail permission), so nothing upstream or in CI prevents it.

Severity note: the audit-side error is in the conservative direction (over-reports risk, never under-reports), so there is no security exposure; the high severity rests on the Permissions tab permanently showing Unknown for the broadest mailbox grant there is and the RBAC-scoping workflow for EWS never visibly converging. remediation.rs:381-397 only passes Graph values and is unaffected. The proposal (carry the role/resource into the resolver or accept ExchangeTarget/(value, role) pairs; fix :341; correct the mod.rs comment; add a unit test) is correct and sufficient.

title: Claims codec mis-models transformation-sourced schema entries: emits TransformationID instead of ID and conflates both on read
rationale: Graph's schema entry for a transformation-sourced claim carries TWO ids: its own `ID` (which `OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId` joins to) and `TransformationID` (which names the transformation). The DTO has one `id`, the writer emits it under `TransformationID` and omits `ID`, so every transformation policy this editor writes has an output claim with nothing to join to (the claim is never emitted). Worse, `parse_schema_entry` reads `ID` first, then `TransformationID`, into the single `id`; an existing Graph policy `{"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationID":"JoinTheData"}` parses as id="DataJoin", loses the transformation reference, and "Save claims" rewrites it as `TransformationID:"DataJoin"` — pointing at a transformation that does not exist. The round-trip test `claims_policy_round_trips_transformation` masks this by using the same string for the schema id, the transformation id and the output ClaimTypeReferenceId. Graph's own example additionally carries `"DataType":"string"` on InputParameters, which `TransformParamDto` drops on round-trip.
proposal: Add `transformation_id: Option<String>` to `ClaimSchemaEntryDto`; in `build_schema_entry` always emit `ID` from `id` and emit `TransformationID` from `transformation_id` when set; in `parse_schema_entry` read `ID` and `TransformationID`/`TransformationId` into their own fields. Add `data_type: Option<String>` to `TransformParamDto` and round-trip it. Replace the masking test with one that uses Graph's documented shape (schema ID "DataJoin", TransformationID "JoinTheData", OutputClaims ClaimTypeReferenceId "DataJoin") and asserts both keys survive parse→build. Fix the DTO doc comments at sso.rs:21/33/91 and the ClaimsEditor to expose the extra field.
verifier_notes: Evidence real. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/claims.rs:46-53 emits the single DTO `id` under `TransformationID` (and omits `ID`) when source==transformation; claims.rs:204 reads `ID` then `TransformationID` into that one field. Microsoft's claims-customization-powershell example is `{"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationId":"JoinTheData","JwtClaimType":"JoinedData"}` with `OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId == "DataJoin"`, and reference-claims-customization states OutputClaims join on the schema entry's ID while TransformationID names the transformation — so a policy written by this codec has no schema ID for the output claim to join to, and an existing policy parses `ID` and drops the transformation reference, then re-saves it as `TransformationID:"DataJoin"`. The round-trip test claims.rs:411-458 uses one string for schema id, transformation id and ClaimTypeReferenceId, masking it. Graph's claimsMappingPolicy resource example carries `"DataType":"string"` on InputParameters, which TransformParamDto (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:69-74 / claims.rs:91,240-243) drops. Two extra tolerances worth adding on read: Microsoft's example uses `TransformationId` casing (the parser reads only `TransformationID`) and the PowerShell page uses a `ClaimsTransformations` (plural) top-level key. No doc/comment argues for the current shape; sso.rs:20-21,32-33,91 restate the wrong model. High is honest: every transformation claim the editor writes is never emitted, and Save corrupts existing policies.
recheck_notes: Confirmed end to end; could not refute. (1) Documented shape: Microsoft Learn (reference-claims-customization; claims-customization-powershell example) shows a transformation-sourced schema entry carrying BOTH keys: {"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationId":"JoinTheData","JwtClaimType":"JoinedData"}, with OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId="DataJoin" joined to the entry's ID. (2) Writer: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/claims.rs:46-53 emits only TransformationID for source=="transformation" and never ID; apply_claims_policy (commands/sso/mod.rs:108-124) passes the string unmodified to GraphClient::create_claims_mapping_policy (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs:7-21), which POSTs it verbatim — no validation or repair anywhere. Reachable in the shipped build via set_claims_mapping (mod.rs:1627-1660, registered in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:192) and create_saml_sso_application (mod.rs:250-252). (3) Reader: claims.rs:204 str_field(obj,&["ID","TransformationID"]) reads ID first, so Microsoft's own example parses as id="DataJoin" and the transformation reference is lost; the TransformationId casing Microsoft's example uses is not read at all. get_sso_config (mod.rs:498-506) feeds this into the editor (web-rs/src/components/claims_editor.rs:199 binds e.id to the single `attribute` field; :320 writes it back), so the UI cannot represent both values. set_claims_mapping then detaches the existing correct policy (mod.rs:1642-1652) and assigns a rewritten one whose entry references a transformation that does not exist — a silent, data-destroying save of a policy the operator never edited. (4) Masking test: claims.rs:411-458 uses one string for the schema id, transformation id and OutputClaims reference and asserts entry.get("ID").is_none(), pinning the wrong behaviour; no repo_invariants test covers the codec. (5) DataType: the Graph claimsMappingPolicy resource example does carry "DataType":"string" on InputParameters and TransformParamDto (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:69-74) drops it, but the reference page lists only ID/Value for InputParameters, so this part is a lossy-round-trip nit rather than the core defect. Severity stays high: not a security exposure, but a correctness bug on a security-critical SSO surface that both writes unusable transformation policies and corrupts existing correct ones on a no-op save.

title: The documented auto-update opt-out (settings.auto_update / AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE) is never consulted; UserSettings::load has no production caller
rationale: The whole `auto_update` field, `default_true`, `auto_update_env_override`, and `UserSettings::load` are dead code: nothing in the backend or frontend reads them, so `check_for_update` always egresses to the GitHub release endpoint on launch. README and DEVELOPMENT.md tell MDM/CI operators the opt-out works, and DEVELOPMENT.md refers to a "settings toggle" that does not exist in web-rs either (no `auto_update` binding or view). title: SSO tab renders an unreadable claims policy as an empty editor; Save then detaches the real policy
rationale: `SsoConfigDto.claims_policy` is `None` both when no policy is assigned AND when the read failed (the DTO doc at crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:297-299 says so). Because `list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies` requires `policy_write_token()`, every operator who has not yet consented `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` sees an EMPTY "Attributes & claims" editor for an app that has a custom policy. Clicking "Save claims" (e.g. to add one claim) triggers the consent flow, then `set_claims_mapping` detaches every existing policy and recreates one from the empty/partial editor — silently deleting the app's configured claims. Nothing in the UI warns that the current state was never loaded.
proposal: Add a discriminator to `SsoConfigDto` (e.g. `claims_policy_unavailable: bool` or `claims_read_error: Option<UiError>`) set in `get_sso_config`'s `Err` arm. In `SsoEditor`, when it is set: render a `Callout tone="warn"` ("Couldn't read the current claims policy — grant consent to load it before editing") with a "Load claims" button that calls `request_scope_consent(.., "policy_write")` and bumps `reload`, and disable "Save claims" until a successful read. Add a GUI test: mock `get_sso_config` with the flag set and assert Save is disabled and no `set_claims_mapping` call happens. Expected effect: no path from an unread policy to a detach.

title: Domain-form tenant id is accepted by the config screen but can never sign in (tid check compares a GUID to the domain)

Add a `sign_in`-level test with a mock `/token` returning a GUID `tid` against a domain-configured service (needs finding on browser-opener injection), and a `settings.rs` test that a domain-configured tenant restores. Alternatively drop domain support from `is_valid_tenant` and say so in the first-run UI; today the two disagree.

title: Mailbox advisory's name-shaped fallback misses MailboxItem.*/MailboxFolder.*/Mail-Advanced.* — org-wide read/write of every mailbox item scores as all-clear

title: list_all_sites drops its truncation signal, so a >5000-site tenant's Sites.Selected sweep is reported and cached as complete
rationale: Every other capped tenant-wide scan in this crate (`list_applications_all`, `list_saml_sso_service_principals`, `collect_all_pages_capped`) returns `(rows, truncated)` precisely so a caller cannot present a partial view as complete. `list_all_sites` is the exception: it silently truncates to `max` and returns a bare Vec. The sweep therefore has no way to know it stopped at site 5000; it sets `total_sites = sites.len()`, `is_complete()` returns true, the result is cached for the audit TTL, and `AppSiteAccessDto::from_sweep` reads an empty match list as 'no per-site grants'. On a tenant with more than 5000 sites, an app's Sites.Selected grants on any site past the cap are invisible and the panel affirmatively says the app has none — the exact 'coverage is never overstated' invariant the surrounding code and sharepoint-selected.md promise. There is no `total_sites >= MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP` check anywhere in the command or the frontend (grep of web-rs for MAX_SITES/5000 finds nothing).
proposal: Change `list_all_sites` to return `Result<(Vec<Site>, bool)>` where the bool is `page.next_link.is_some() || pages hit MAX_PAGES` when the cap stops the walk (mirror `collect_all_pages_capped`'s tail logic, or add a scoped `collect_pages_from_capped` helper and reuse it here). In `sweep_site_permissions` bind the flag, add `truncated: bool` to `SiteSweepResult`/`AppSiteAccessDto` (additive field), fold it into `is_complete()` (`!cancelled && sites_failed == 0 && !truncated`), skip caching when truncated, and render the existing `IndexCapNotice` pattern in the Sites tab. Add a wiremock test where page 1 already exceeds `max` and assert `truncated == true`.
verifier_notes: Premise verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:74-107: `list_all_sites(max)` loops `while out.len() < max`, then `out.truncate(max); Ok(out)` — no truncation flag, unlike `collect_all_pages_capped` (transport.rs:229-262) which returns `(Vec, bool)`. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sharepoint.rs:842-845 binds `sites`/`total = sites.len()`; :977-992 builds `SiteSweepResult{total_sites: total, cancelled, sites_failed}` and caches when `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0`; crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sharepoint.rs:130-132 `is_complete()` = `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0`. No `truncated` field exists on `SiteSweepResult`/`AppSiteAccessDto` (dto/sharepoint.rs:64-96). Frontend: web-rs/src/components/app_site_access_panel.rs:242 keys the 'no grants' wording off `is_complete()`; web-rs/src/views/resource_access/sites.rs:113-131 prints 'scanned X of Y' with only failed/cancelled qualifiers; grep of web-rs for MAX_SITES/5000 finds nothing. The only acknowledgement is the comment at commands/sharepoint.rs:756-758 ('Raise if a user legitimately hits it') — but nothing tells the user or the code that it was hit. This directly violates the repo's own stated invariants (sharepoint.rs:825-828 'coverage is never overstated'; AGENTS.md 'empty = no grants only when is_complete()'; 'a truncated run is never cached'). docs/architecture/sharepoint-selected.md never mentions the cap. `IndexCapNotice` exists (web-rs/src/components/index_cap_notice.rs:48) for reuse. Existing test `list_all_sites_follows_next_link_on_sharepoint_scope` (tests/sharepoint.rs:154) does not cover the cap. title: create_application returns Err after the app registration was already created, so no cache is invalidated and a retry creates a duplicate
rationale: caching-and-search.md's rule for multi-step mutations is "a partial success is a real write — invalidate, gated on 'something actually changed'", which `downgrade_application_permission_core`, `remove_expired_passwords` and the bulk commands obey. Here `POST /applications` succeeds, then a 403/429 from `ensure_service_principal` (or `add_password`) propagates via `?`; the command returns Err and `invalidate_app_lists` never runs. `apps_pairing`, `app_name_index` and `search_corpus` are pinned (LRU cannot evict them) with a 60-minute TTL, so the App Registrations list and global search do not show the new app, the operator sees only an error, and the natural retry creates a second registration with the same display name (Entra allows duplicates). `bulk_create` avoids this only because it passes `..Default::default()` (no SP, no secret).
proposal: Give `create_application_core` the shape `downgrade_application_permission_core` already has: return `Ok((CreateApplicationResult, Option<UiError>))` (or add `error: Option<UiError>` to `CreateApplicationResult`) once `create_application` has landed, collecting SP/secret failures instead of `?`-ing them; in the command, call `invalidate_app_lists` whenever `application` exists and then surface the error. Update `bulk.rs:570` and `restore.rs:218` callers (both already tolerate per-item errors). Add a wiremock handler test (POST /applications 201, POST /servicePrincipals 403) asserting `apps_pairing`/`app_name_index` are dropped and the error is returned.
verifier_notes: Evidence is real: applications/mod.rs:322-323 `create_application_core(..).await?` then `invalidate_app_lists`; mod.rs:338 POST lands, mod.rs:343-347 `ensure_service_principal(..).await?` and mod.rs:356 `add_password(..).await?` propagate after the registration exists. UI reaches it: views/dialogs/create_app_dialog.rs:54 sends `create_service_principal: csp` (rest `..Default::default()`). `ensure_service_principal` (graph service_principals.rs:506-516) has no replication retry, while sso/mod.rs:52-72 exists precisely because a create-then-reference call can fail right after a POST — so the partial path is reachable in practice, not just under 403/429. Consequence checked: apps_pairing/app_name_index/search_corpus are pinned (cache.rs:214-222, 296-304; mod.rs:220) so only TTL or the list's explicit Refresh (application_list.rs:249 `invalidate_list_cache`) recovers; restore.rs:213-235 also treats the Err as 'not created' so a re-run restore would duplicate too. bulk.rs:566-570 is safe only via `..Default::default()`. caching-and-search.md 'a partial success is a real write — invalidate' names `downgrade_application_permission` as the model (permissions.rs:887-890). Severity downgraded from high to medium: the operator gets an error, the app exists, and the list Refresh button busts the cache; the duplicate-on-retry is real but is clutter (an orphan finding), not a security regression.

title: get_application_detail caches a degraded permission resolution: a transient failure resolving one resource SP marks all of that resource's permissions as not granted for the 60-minute TTL

With `live_sp == None` both join closures return `None`, so every `ResolvedPermission` for that resource carries `runtime_assignment_id: None` / `runtime_grant_id: None`, which the Permissions tab renders as not granted and offers to grant. The detail is then stored unconditionally under `app_detail_key` for the Lists TTL. AGENTS.md says a degraded run is never cached nor shown as all-clear; here a permission that IS granted is shown as absent, and only the operator's manual Refresh clears it. `resolve_resource_sp` itself caches only `Ok`, so the graph layer got this right and the command layer undid it.

title: score_one swallows a failed SP lookup, skips the org-wide reconciliation, and the run still caches as a clean complete scan
rationale: When the lean lookup fails (Graph 5xx after retries, or a task that runs after the LRU seed was evicted — `seed_lean_sps_from_index` caps at the bucket size), `sp` is `None` but scoring continues: Rule 4 (disabled SP) and Rule 3 (admin consent) lose their input, and — more importantly — `orgwide` is empty so `resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached` can return a `Scoped { Rbac }` verdict that is never reconciled against a surviving org-wide grant. That is exactly the under-report the AuditCoverageGap::GraphAppRoleAssignments doc (dto/audit.rs:141-146) calls out, yet here nothing is added to `degraded`, so the run passes `run_is_cacheable` and is served from cache as authoritative. Contrast `ResourceResolver.unresolved`, which exists precisely to flag the equivalent hole for resource indexes.
proposal: Either return `Err(err.into())` from score_one on a failed SP lookup (it classifies as Transient → `unscored` → `PerPrincipalScoring`, and a dead session is caught by the same match), or add an `sp_unresolved: AtomicBool` to ScoreCtx and push a new `AuditCoverageGap::ServicePrincipalLookup` when set. In both cases skip the Exchange probe when `sp` is `None` (reconciliation is impossible, so the reduced weight must not be awarded).
verifier_notes: audit.rs:1489-1499 maps a failed `get_service_principal_by_app_id_lean` to `None` with only a warn; the lean lookup propagates Graph errors via `?` (service_principals.rs lean fn, `get_json(...).await?`), so a 5xx after the retry budget lands here. With `sp = None`, `orgwide` is `HashSet::new()` (:1527-1541) and `resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached` (mail_scopes.rs:228-253 → `reconcile_orgwide_grant` at :173) can no longer defeat a `Scoped` verdict — precisely the under-report `AuditCoverageGap::GraphAppRoleAssignments` documents (dto/audit.rs:141-146). Nothing pushes to `degraded` on this path (contrast `unscored` → `PerPrincipalScoring` at :393-396 and `resolver.had_unresolved()` → `PermissionResolution` at :402-404), so `run_is_cacheable` (:445) passes and the run is cached as complete, against the AGENTS.md "degraded run is never cached" rule. Rare in practice (the SP index seeds most lookups; `seed_lean_sps_from_index` caps at the bucket size, service_principals.rs:296-297), so medium not high. Returning `Err` (→ `Transient` via `classify_audit_failure`, audit.rs:65-73) is the minimal fix consistent with the existing shape.

title: Managed Identities 'Refresh' invalidates only `{tenant}|mi`, but the list is rebuilt from the untouched shared SP index — refresh is a no-op
rationale: `list_managed_identities` was refactored to derive from `sp_index_cached`, but the per-page Refresh invalidation for MIs was not updated. title: Managed-identity Azure RBAC view duplicates management-group-inherited assignments once per subscription
rationale: The per-subscription `principalId eq` query returns assignments ABOVE the subscription too (management group / root). The command fans out over every reachable subscription and flattens without deduplicating, so a managed identity holding Reader at a management group over N subscriptions renders N identical rows (same `RoleAssignment.id`, same scope), each tagged with a different subscription display name. `scope_level` explicitly classifies "Management group" scopes, so these rows are expected output — and they are wrong by a factor of N. For an operator reviewing MI privilege this both inflates the count and hides the fact that it is a single inherited grant.
proposal: Dedupe `flat` by `RoleAssignment.id` (fall back to `(scope, role_definition_id, principal_id)` when id is None) with a `HashSet` before role-name resolution; for an assignment whose scope is above the subscription, label `subscription` as "(inherited)" or the MG name rather than the first subscription that happened to return it. Extract a pure `dedupe_assignments(Vec<(String, RoleAssignment)>) -> Vec<(String, RoleAssignment)>` and unit-test with one MG assignment returned by two subscriptions.
verifier_notes: Evidence real. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/managed_identity.rs:213-258 fans out `list_role_assignments_for_principal` per subscription and flattens with no dedupe; there is no HashSet on assignment id anywhere (the only HashSet in managed_identity_detail_pane.rs:115 tracks visited tabs). crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:55-57 says 'at or below', but Microsoft's Role Assignments API doc says `$filter=principalId eq {id}` returns assignments 'at, above or below the scope' — so a management-group (or root) assignment is returned once per subscription queried. `scope_level` (managed_identity.rs:420-424) explicitly labels 'Management group', confirming such rows are expected output, yet each is tagged with whichever subscription returned it. `RoleAssignment.id` is `Option<String>` (arm/src/models.rs:73-77) so the proposed fallback key is needed. No doc or comment treats the duplication as deliberate. Medium is fair for an N-fold inflated privilege view.

title: orgwide_mailbox_grant folds a failed Graph read into EntraReach::NotHeld, yielding a definitive no_access for managed identities on a transient error
rationale: Three distinct Graph failures collapse into "not held". Combined with RbacReach::None{had_assignments:false} (the managed-identity / not-in-EXO-store case, which rbac_reach_for returns for a missing-object error), synthesize produces verdict no_access and the detail states positively that no Entra grant exists. The sibling sharepoint_grants_held (884-887) explicitly distinguishes unreadable from none; the mailbox side does not. The same helper feeds the `exchange_client` failure branch (379-397) where None becomes a generic unknown, so only the main path is affected.
proposal: Return a tri-state (e.g. `Result<Vec<String>, ()>` or an enum Held(Vec)/None/Unreadable) and add `EntraReach::Unreadable`, scored at level 1 (unknown) in synthesize with detail "Entra app-role assignments couldn't be read". Reuse mail_scopes::held_orgwide_mail_grants for the body (see the duplication finding) once it, too, exposes read failure. Add a synthesize test: Unreadable + RbacReach::None{false} => verdict unknown, not no_access.
verifier_notes: Verified: orgwide_mailbox_grant (permission_tester.rs:63-93) returns None for `get_service_principal_by_app_id` Err or Ok(None) (`.ok()??` at :70-73), for mailbox_resource_roles Err (:76) and for list_app_role_assignments Err (:77) — the docstring at :58-60 even says 'or can't be resolved'. test_mailbox_access maps None straight to EntraReach::NotHeld (:404-411) and synthesize writes 'No organization-wide Graph mailbox permission is granted in Entra ID.' (:264-266). With RbacReach::None{had_assignments:false} — which rbac_reach_for returns for a missing-object error (:161-166, the managed-identity / not-in-EXO-store case) — the verdict is `no_access`. The SharePoint sibling sharepoint_grants_held (:882-884) documents the opposite contract, and the exchange_client-failure branch (:379-397) already turns None into unknown, so the asymmetry is real. docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:76-95 describes the Entra layer but never states that an unreadable assignment list should read as not-held, so this is not a documented decision. Proposal is sound; note that Ok(None) from the SP lookup (SP genuinely absent) should stay NotHeld — only the Err paths become Unreadable. held_orgwide_mail_grants (mail_scopes.rs:48-73) has the same fold-to-empty shape but there empty is the safe (org-wide) direction, so only the tester side is wrong.

title: find_mailbox_reachers discovers candidates from the Microsoft Graph resource only, so an app whose sole mailbox grant is org-wide EWS full_access_as_app is missed or reported as no_access
rationale: The reverse lookup answers "who can reach this mailbox?". A principal granted only full_access_as_app (full access to every mailbox over EWS) is not a Graph appRoleAssignedTo hit; if it is registered in Exchange's SP store it enters with empty held permissions and, absent an RBAC assignment, reads no_access — the strongest possible mailbox grant reported as none. The single-app tester and the audit both already close this gap, so the two surfaces disagree for the same principal.
proposal: Replace graph_role_index + one appRoleAssignedTo read with mailbox_resource_roles (both resource SPs) and page list_app_role_assigned_to on each, filtering with is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission(Some(resource.app_id), value); or, simpler, reuse prefetch_ews_full_access_grants' shape to add EWS holders to `candidates` with held = ["full_access_as_app"]. Extend merge test to cover an EWS-only candidate.
verifier_notes: Verified: find_mailbox_reachers builds candidates from graph_role_index + one list_app_role_assigned_to on the Graph SP only (permission_tester.rs:466-479) and filters with Some(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID) (:476); merge_exchange_candidates (:687-699) adds EXO-store principals with an empty held list; probe_candidate then sets EntraReach::NotHeld when held is empty (:800-806), so an EWS-only principal with no RBAC assignment reads `no_access` (or is absent entirely when not in Exchange's SP store). The single-app tester (:71-79) and the audit's prefetch_ews_full_access_grants (audit.rs:1007-1040) both already read the Office 365 Exchange Online SP for exactly this grant, and docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:60-61 claims the probe uses 'the same two-layer union the Permission tester uses' — which is currently untrue for the candidate discovery step. No doc or comment names the Graph-only sweep as deliberate. Proposal (page appRoleAssignedTo on both mailbox resources via mailbox_resource_roles, or reuse prefetch_ews_full_access_grants' shape, and extend the merge test at :1511) is feasible; a tenant with no EWS-consenting app has no SPO/EXO SP, which must read as an ordinary empty set, as audit.rs:1015-1021 does.

title: test_site_access claims "holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant" when the grants read actually failed
rationale: When sharepoint_grants_held returns None (SP lookup or appRoleAssignments read failed), path 1 is silently skipped and, if no permission entry exists on the chain, the command returns a definitive no_access whose detail asserts a fact it never established. An app holding org-wide Sites.Read.All reads as having no access during a transient Graph failure — the exact under-report the doc forbids, and the Exchange half of the same file already avoids (RbacReach::Indeterminate).
proposal: Extract a pure site_verdict(held, hit, label) and return `unknown` when the grants could not be READ and no entry exists — but distinguish the two things sharepoint_grants_held currently folds into None (permission_tester.rs:888-893): `get_service_principal_by_app_id` returning Ok(None) (the SP genuinely does not exist in this tenant, so `no_access` is the right answer) versus an Err on the SP lookup / graph_role_index / list_app_role_assignments (unreadable → `unknown`). Return a tri-state (or Result<Option<..>>) from sharepoint_grants_held so the verdict table has: org-wide wins; unreadable + no entry → unknown; unreadable + entry → unknown (already at :1113-1123); no SP → no_access; entry + matching scope → scoped; entry without scope → no_access naming required_scope_for.
verifier_notes: Evidence is real: permission_tester.rs:1067 reads `held` once; path 1 at :1077-1089 is skipped whenever held is None; :1091-1101 then returns a definitive `no_access` whose detail asserts 'it holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant'; only the entry-found branch handles None (:1113-1123). The docstring on sharepoint_grants_held (:882-884) and on HeldSharePointGrants (:857-859) both say None must be reported as unknown, and docs/architecture/sharepoint-selected.md:103 states 'A failure to read the assignments reports `unknown`, never "no access"' — so this is a contract breach, not a decision. No unit test covers the branch (tests module :1230-1535 has no test_site_access assembly tests). Severity adjusted from high to medium: the false negative requires a Graph failure on the SP/assignment reads while the site resolve and chain walk succeed (a narrow, transient window), and the fix is an hour's work. The proposal needs one correction: `??` at :888-892 also maps a non-existent SP to None, and for that case `no_access` is correct, so the tri-state must keep it apart from a read failure.

title: list_app_role_resources is cached with "no mutation-driven invalidation" although the App roles tab mutates exactly what it lists
rationale: `list_tenant_app_role_resources` returns tenant-owned SPs exposing an enabled Application role plus a role count. `upsert_enterprise_app_role`/`delete_enterprise_app_role` change that set (first Application role added, last one disabled), and `create_application`/`delete_application` add or remove the SP. None of them drop `{tenant}|app_role_resources`, so the Grant-access picker's "Tenant app registrations" group (permission_picker.rs:119) omits a freshly published API, keeps a deleted app, and shows stale counts for up to 60 minutes. The graph crate already busts its own `resource:` prefix on the same writes for the same reason (applications.rs:622-625); the command-side list was not given the same treatment.
proposal: Move `app_role_resources_key` into `applications/cache.rs`; drop it inside `invalidate_app_lists`, and add a targeted `cache.invalidate(CacheKind::Lists, &app_role_resources_key(tenant))` on the Ok path of `upsert_enterprise_app_role` and `delete_enterprise_app_role`. Extend `detail_cache_tests` with an assertion that `invalidate_app_lists` drops it. Fix the doc comment.
verifier_notes: permissions.rs:26-28 `app_role_resources_key` is private to the module; :68 `cache.put(CacheKind::Lists, key, &rows)`; the doc comment at :39-41 claims 'read-only directory ... no mutation-driven invalidation is wired'. But the app mutates the set: app_roles.rs:336-339 and :365 `invalidate_app_details` only (which sweeps `app_detail|`/`mail_scopes|` prefixes, cache.rs:83-90), and `invalidate_app_lists` (cache.rs:107-133) has no `app_role_resources` key; grep confirms nothing else touches it. The graph crate busts its own `resource:` prefix on the same write (applications.rs:622-625), so the command-side list is the odd one out. permission_picker.rs:112-122 loads it once per wizard open with no Refresh affordance and renders the 'Tenant app registrations' optgroup (:190). The documented rationale is unsound (the directory is mutated by this app), so it does not refute. Medium is fair: an operator who exposes a new Application role and immediately opens Grant access won't find the API for up to an hour.

title: grant_single_permission_core and grant_admin_consent_core return Err after real writes (manifest PATCH, SP creation) so the command layer never invalidates
rationale: In the single-grant core the `requiredResourceAccess` PATCH lands, then `ensure_service_principal` (creates an SP, a new Enterprise App row) or `resolve_resource_sp` fails with `?`. The command receives Err and busts nothing: the cached detail shows the old manifest, and a newly created SP is missing from `sp_index`/enterprise/search for the TTL. In the admin-consent core the SP is created and then the idempotency `try_join` fails (a 403 on `oauth2PermissionGrants` for an operator without `DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All` is realistic); same outcome. The repo already solved this exact shape in `downgrade_application_permission_core` and its doc comment explains why; the two grant cores predate it.
proposal: Adopt the `(outcome, Option<UiError>)` return in both grant cores: once the manifest PATCH or `ensure_service_principal` has landed, collect later errors instead of `?`, and have `grant_single_permission` / `grant_admin_consent` (and the bulk/restore callers) invalidate on `manifest_changed || sp_created` before surfacing the error. Mirror the two `downgrade` tests for these cores with wiremock.
verifier_notes: permissions.rs:635-643 PATCHes `requiredResourceAccess`, then :648 `ensure_service_principal(..).await?`, :649-656 `resolve_resource_sp(..).await?` / `ok_or_else(..)?`, and :665 `list_app_role_assignments(..).await?` after a possibly-created SP — all propagate as Err, and grant_single_permission (:578-588) invalidates only on Ok. grant_admin_consent_core :394 creates the SP then :408-412 `try_join(..).await?`; grant_admin_consent (:344-353) likewise. The repo already solved this shape with the `(outcome, Option<UiError>)` return and doc comment at :887-890 / :846-855. The bulk caller has the same gap: bulk.rs:470-482 maps a core Err to `sp_created: false`, and :513-517 busts nothing if no other app granted, so a created SP stays out of sp_index/enterprise/search for the TTL. restore.rs:274 also tolerates per-item Err without recording sp creation. Medium is right: stale detail/enterprise rows for up to 60 min after a real write, recoverable by Refresh.

title: Readiness scope probe keeps a hardcoded CAE list that has drifted from the capabilities catalog (group_membership probed non-CAE)
rationale: The catalog carries `scope_feature: Some("group_membership")` (capabilities.rs:308) and `AppState::ensure_group_member_token` acquires it with `cae = true` (state.rs:630-645), but this list omits `group_membership`, so the readiness page pre-warms a non-CAE token for a Graph scope set. state.rs:563-568 states the invariant this breaks: 'cae MUST match the CAE-ness of the adapter that later consumes the same scope set: the token cache key omits CAE-ness, so a non-CAE pre-warm would make a new_cae adapter reuse a non-CAE token'. The same list also names `sync` and `policy_write`, which no catalog entry probes, showing it is maintained by hand and nothing pins it.
proposal: Move CAE-ness next to the scope set: have `AppState::consent_scopes_for` return `(Vec<String>, bool /*cae*/)` (or add a `cae: bool` column to a small feature table) and make both `ensure_scoped_token` wrappers and `probe_scope` read it. Delete the `is_graph` match. Add a unit test asserting every catalog `scope_feature` resolves through `consent_scopes_for`.
verifier_notes: readiness.rs:276-279 hardcodes `"write" | "sync" | "audit_log" | "policy" | "policy_write" | "sharepoint"` while the catalog carries `scope_feature: Some("group_membership")` (capabilities.rs:308) and `ensure_group_member_token` acquires it with `cae = true` (state.rs:630-637). readiness.rs:56-66 probes every distinct catalog `scope_feature`, so `group_membership` is probed through the non-CAE `access_token_for_scopes` branch. The token cache is keyed only by `(tenant_id, scope_key)` (token_cache.rs:120-128; service/mod.rs:396-419 pass different `claims` but the same scopes), so the readiness pre-warm seeds a non-CAE token that the `new_cae` group-member adapter (state.rs:465) then reuses — the invariant state.rs:563-568 spells out in caps. `sync` and `policy_write` in the list have no catalog `scope_feature`, confirming hand maintenance; nothing in tests/ references `is_graph` or `probe_scope`. Practical blast radius is a Graph token without cp1 (CAE revocation delayed until expiry, not a hard failure), so medium rather than high. Proposal to co-locate CAE-ness with `consent_scopes_for` is sound.

title: Redundant-permissions Fix silently drops values whose covering permission is vetoed — doc says they land in `skipped`, and the UI then clears the Fix button
rationale: The handler's fail-closed comment (remediation.rs:373-377) promises: 'skipping it costs the operator a re-run once Exchange answers, and the value shows up in `skipped` saying so'. But when every covering permission is vetoed (`Err(_) => HashMap::new()` at :401 for a non-Exchange-admin, or a transient Exchange failure via `.unwrap_or_default()` at :399) the loop hits `continue` without `skipped.push`. The command returns `Ok { removed: [], skipped: [] }`; `RedundantPermsAction` (web-rs row.rs:377-395) then toasts 'Removed 0 redundant permissions' and calls `on_done`, which `retain`s the RemoveRedundantPermissions button away while the finding and the live permission remain. An operator without Exchange RBAC rights can never see why the Fix did nothing.
proposal: In `plan_redundant_removals`, collect the pre-veto broaders first; if non-empty but the post-veto set is empty, push the value into `skipped` (or a new `vetoed: Vec<String>` on `RedundantPermissionsOutcome` with a reason string). In the UI, only fire `on_done` when `removed` is non-empty, and render the veto reason ('could not confirm the covering permission is org-wide — Exchange unavailable'). Add a planner test for the all-vetoed case.
verifier_notes: remediation.rs:256-264: broaders are filtered by `!broader_is_confined(...)` and an empty post-veto set hits `continue` with no `skipped.push`, contradicting the handler's own comment at :373-377 ("the value shows up in `skipped` saying so"). With `Err(_) => HashMap::new()` (:401) or `.unwrap_or_default()` (:399), `broader_is_confined` (:403-408) returns true for every Graph mail permission, so a non-Exchange-admin gets `Ok { removed: [], skipped: [] }`. The scorer, by contrast, treats an empty `mail_scopes` as org-wide (scoring.rs:47-48, :274-275) and DOES raise the finding. UI: row.rs:377-395 toasts "Removed 0 redundant permissions ... re-run the audit" and calls `on_done` unconditionally on `Ok`, and row.rs:127-129 wires that to clear the remediation kind from the row, so the Fix button disappears while the finding and grant remain. None of the planner tests at remediation.rs:573-660 pass a vetoing closure, so the all-vetoed case is untested. Proposal is correct.

title: Restore reports a failed Graph read as a confident runbook fact ('not found in destination' / 'app had none in the backup')
rationale: If `list_managed_identities` fails (throttled, 403 for a role that lacks directory read, or a session that died mid-restore), `unwrap_or_default()` yields an empty list and EVERY managed identity is reported as "not found in the destination — recreate via IaC", sending the infra team to recreate identities that already exist. Likewise a transient `Err` from `get_service_principal_by_app_id` is reported as "the app had none in the backup", which is false when `has_service_principal` was true. The rubric's "result that misleads the operator" case; and because these two passes never note failures on the `SessionDead` latch, a dead session in Pass 4/5 produces a full page of wrong runbook items rather than the `session_expired` flag.
proposal: In `restore_managed_identities`, match on the list result: on `Err(e)` call `session.note_code(e.ui_code())` (thread `&SessionDead` into the function), push ONE `ManualItem`/warning "could not enumerate destination managed identities: {e} — re-binding skipped" and return, instead of emitting per-MI 'not found' items. In `restore_enterprise_app`, split the arm: `Ok(None)` keeps the current text, `Err(e)` pushes "could not read service principal: {e}" and notes the session code. Add the same `note_code` to the tag/patch/assign/group-member failures in that function so Pass 4 latches like Pass 2. Unit-test the MI branch with a wiremock 500 on `/servicePrincipals` asserting no per-MI 'not found' item is produced. Effort S.
verifier_notes: Both sites are as quoted. restore.rs:734 `list_managed_identities().await.unwrap_or_default()` turns any Err into an empty map, so :740-753 emits a per-MI 'not found in the destination — recreate via IaC' item for every MI. restore.rs:653-661 collapses `Ok(None)` and `Err(_)` into 'the app had none in the backup'. Neither `restore_enterprise_app` (:623-720) nor `restore_managed_identities` (:723+) takes `&SessionDead` or calls `note_code`, whereas `wire_application` does (:412, :580, :603). Consequence for the latch: the Pass 4 loop (:296-304) checks `session.is_dead()` but nothing inside Pass 4 can set it, so a session dying during Pass 4 produces one false 'had no SP' item per remaining enterprise app and `report.session_expired` stays false (:327). Severity adjusted to medium rather than high: `list_managed_identities` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/service_principals.rs:108-120) is a paged read behind the shared retry budget and Pass 5 only starts when the session is alive (:313), so the trigger window is a session death or budget exhaustion inside passes 4-5 — narrower than the reviewer implies — but when it fires the output is a confidently wrong DR runbook, which is exactly the misleading-result class. Proposal is small and feasible (`SessionDead` is a `pub(crate)` Arc<AtomicBool> in commands/dispatch.rs:29, trivially threaded).

title: Restore is not idempotent, yet its own report instructs the operator to re-run it
evidence:
restore.rs:748-753 `reason: format!(
    "Managed identity ({}{}) not found in the destination. Recreate it via your \
     infrastructure-as-code, then re-run the restore to re-bind its Graph \
     app-roles.",`
restore.rs:197-231 Pass 1 `for app in &backup.app_registrations { ... match create_application_core(&client, input).await { Ok(res) => { app_id_remap.insert(...); created.push(...) }` — no lookup of an existing app by name/identifier URI/marker before creating.
restore.rs:588-590 `for meta in &app.secrets { ... match client.add_password(&c.new_object_id, &name, lifetime).await {`
web-rs/src/views/dr.rs confirm modal: "This creates new app registrations in the current tenant and regenerates their secrets. It does not overwrite or delete anything that already exists."
rationale: `restore_tenant` unconditionally creates a shell for every app registration in the manifest and mints fresh secrets for each. The MI runbook item explicitly tells the operator to "re-run the restore" after recreating the identities via IaC. Following that instruction duplicates every app registration (same display names, `api://` URIs rewritten to a second appId, second set of live 180-day secrets, second admin consent) in the destination tenant. There is no dry-run warning either: `plan_restore` does not look at the destination at all.
proposal: Two tiers. (S, removes the harm) Reword the ManualItem at restore.rs:748-753 and the arch doc sentence at docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:203 so they no longer say 're-run the restore'; add a 'Re-bind managed identities only' action that runs just `restore_managed_identities` (Pass 5) against a loaded manifest, and make `plan_restore` warn when `!tenant_changed`. (M, optional) Adoption-aware Pass 1 via a marker — note the core `Application` model has no `tags` field today (only `ServicePrincipal.tags`, crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/models.rs:165), so this needs the model and `AppPatch` extended plus a destination lookup; count adoptions in `RestoreReport`.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: Pass 1 (restore.rs:197-231) calls `create_application_core` for every manifest app with no lookup of an existing app (grep for existing/already/adopt/idempot in restore.rs finds only comments); secrets are minted per created app (restore.rs:588-598); the ManualItem at :748-753 and the architecture doc at backup-and-restore.md:203 both instruct 'recreate ... then re-run'. Severity trimmed from high to medium: the confirm modal (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:414-415) states plainly that restore 'creates new app registrations ... does not overwrite or delete anything', so the operator is warned that a re-run creates, and the defect is the instruction text rather than silent behaviour. The S-sized fix (reword + MI-only re-bind) removes the harm; the tag-based adoption is a larger design change and is better framed as an enhancement.

title: Site sweep silently truncates at MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP and caches the result as complete; is_complete() has no truncation dimension (the audit result does)
rationale: A tenant with more than 5 000 enumerable sites gets total_sites = 5000, sites_scanned = 5000, sites_failed = 0 → cached for 60 minutes and is_complete() = true. The per-app panel then states "no per-site grants" for an app whose grants live on site 5 001+, and the CSV coverage line claims full coverage — the exact overstatement the sweep's own comments promise never to make. Nothing tells the operator the cap was hit, so "Raise if a user legitimately hits it" can never be acted on.
proposal: Make list_all_sites return `(Vec<Site>, truncated: bool)` (fetch until len > max or nextLink exhausted, then truncate and flag), add `truncated: bool` to SiteSweepResult / AppSiteAccessDto, include `!self.truncated` in is_complete(), exclude truncated runs from the cache (or cache with the flag), and render "more than 5 000 sites — coverage is partial" in the summary and export. Add a DTO test mirroring the audit's truncated case.
verifier_notes: Verified: MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP = 5_000 with the 'Raise if a user legitimately hits it' comment (sharepoint.rs:756-758) is passed to list_all_sites (:843); the graph client stops paging at `out.len() < max` and `out.truncate(max)` with no signal (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:87-106); the sweep caches on `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` (:988-992) and SiteSweepResult/AppSiteAccessDto::is_complete is `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` (dto/sharepoint.rs:130-132), whereas the audit's AuditExportCoverage::is_complete includes `!self.truncated` (dto/audit.rs:125-127). The UI summary reads 'scanned X of Y sites' with Y == total == 5000 and no cap mention (web-rs views/resource_access/sites.rs:115-123), the export reuses that sentence (:144-149), and neither sharepoint-selected.md nor CHANGELOG.md mentions the cap. So a >5000-site tenant gets a cached, is_complete()==true result and the per-app panel's 'no per-site grants' overstates coverage — contradicting the 'coverage is never overstated' promise at sharepoint.rs:826-829 and sharepoint-selected.md:30-34. Not a documented decision. Proposal is right; prefer caching WITH the truncated flag (and letting is_complete carry it) over excluding truncated runs from the cache, otherwise a large tenant re-sweeps 5000 sites on every panel visit.

title: OIDC create leaves the client-secret lifetime unbounded, unlike the SAML cert lifetime and the rotation path
rationale: `secret_lifetime_days` is caller-supplied and reaches `add_password` unchecked: `0` mints a secret that is already expired when the summary shows it; an absurd value hits Graph's rejection only AFTER `instantiate_application_template` has created the app+SP, producing exactly the half-configured app the SAML path pre-validates `cert_lifetime_days` to avoid. The sibling `rotate_app_credential` clamps to 1..=730, so the same concept has two policies in the same crate.
proposal: Add `resolve_secret_lifetime_days(Option<u32>) -> Result<u32, UiError>` (typed `invalid_secret_lifetime`, bounds 1..=730 shared as a `core` constant with `keyvault.rs`), call it in `create_oidc_sso_application` before `instantiate_application_template`, and reuse the value in `configure_oidc`. One table test mirroring `a_signing_certificate_lifetime_is_bounded_by_entras_three_year_ceiling`.
verifier_notes: Evidence real and the failure mode is worse than stated. sso/mod.rs:351-358 takes `input.secret_lifetime_days.unwrap_or(180)` with no bounds, while the SAML path gates `cert_lifetime_days` via `resolve_cert_lifetime_days` before instantiate (mod.rs:149-152, 415-427) and keyvault.rs:85 clamps 1..=730 — two policies for one concept. The wizard field is a free-text `<Input value=secret_days />` parsed as u32 (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dialogs/sso_wizard_dialog.rs:58,195,319) with no min/max. Downstream, `GraphClient::add_password` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/credentials.rs:38-39) computes `chrono::Utc::now() + chrono::Duration::from_std(lifetime)`; for u32::MAX days (~11.7M years) that addition overflows chrono's date range and panics rather than returning a Graph 400 — inside the command, after `instantiate_application_template` has already created the app+SP. `0` yields an already-expired secret. Proposal (shared typed bound, checked before instantiate, reused in `configure_oidc`, table test) is consistent with the existing SAML pattern. Medium is fair.

title: set_claims_mapping leaks one orphan claimsMappingPolicy per save and swallows the listing error
rationale: `remove_claims_mapping_policy` is a `$ref` DELETE — it unassigns but never deletes the tenant-level `claimsMappingPolicy` object, and every save then POSTs a fresh one via `apply_claims_policy`. A tenant accumulates one orphan under `/policies/claimsMappingPolicies` per "Save claims" click, forever, with the operator's display name on each. The comment's premise ("effectively replace-only") is wrong: Graph documents Update (PATCH) for claimsMappingPolicy, so the existing policy's `definition` can be replaced in place — no detach→assign window during which tokens carry default claims either. Separately, `if let Ok(existing)` turns a transient listing failure into an attempt to assign a second policy, which Graph rejects (one per SP) with an opaque 400.
proposal: Add `update_claims_mapping_policy(id, definition_json)` (PATCH /policies/claimsMappingPolicies/{id}) and `delete_claims_mapping_policy(id)` to crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs. In `set_claims_mapping` (sso/mod.rs:1628-1664): propagate the listing error with `?` instead of `if let Ok`. When exactly one policy is assigned, read its `appliesTo` (or count assignments) first: PATCH its definition in place only if this SP is its sole subject; if the policy is shared with other SPs, fall back to unassign + create + assign (editing a shared policy in place would change claims for every other app). When the new policy is empty, unassign then DELETE the old policy only if `appliesTo` is now empty. Also apply the same ownership check before deleting in the create flow's failure path. CHANGELOG entry for the removed orphan accumulation.
verifier_notes: Premise confirmed: sso/mod.rs:1642-1650 calls `remove_claims_mapping_policy`, which is a `$ref` DELETE (policies.rs:60-72, unassign only); `apply_claims_policy` (mod.rs:104-121) then POSTs a fresh policy on every save, and policies.rs exposes only create/assign/list/remove — no update or delete. Microsoft's claimsMappingPolicy resource page lists Update and Delete methods, so the docstring's "effectively replace-only" (mod.rs:1623-1624) is wrong, and docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:89 records no rationale for orphaning. `if let Ok(existing)` at mod.rs:1643 does swallow a transient listing failure and proceeds to assign a second policy. What the proposal missed: Microsoft documents that one claims-mapping policy may be assigned to multiple service principals, so an unconditional PATCH-in-place would silently alter other apps' claims — the in-place path needs an `appliesTo` guard (the reviewer only mentioned it for DELETE). Medium is fair.

title: ConcurrencyThrottle halves only once under sustained 429 pressure because the window re-anchors on every event
rationale: `HALVE_WINDOW_SECS` is documented as the 'Minimum seconds between cap halvings', but `*last = Some(now)` runs before the `within_window` early return, so a suppressed event still moves the anchor. With 4-8 lanes each receiving 429s more often than every 2s (the normal shape of a Graph throttle storm) `within` is true for every event after the first, and the cap goes 8→4 and stays there — the 'degrade to per-object reads / floor at 1' behaviour never engages. The existing paused-clock test only fires bursts at a single instant and then advances past the window, so it cannot see this.
proposal: Track two instants: `last_throttle` (updated on every event; drives the recovery quiet check) and `last_halved` (updated only when `next < prev`; drives the halving window). Add a `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` that fires `on_throttle` every 1s for 10s on `new(8)` and asserts the limit reaches `MIN_CONCURRENCY`.
verifier_notes: throttle.rs:102-104 sets `*last = Some(now)` unconditionally before the `within_window` early return at :106, so the anchor slides on every suppressed 429 and a stream of events spaced <2s apart never halves past the first 8→4. The struct doc at :41-43 ("halves ... at most once per HALVE_WINDOW_SECS") and the const doc at :21 ("Minimum seconds between cap halvings") both promise repeated halvings under sustained pressure, so this is a real divergence, not a documented decision. The transport fires `on_throttle` on every 429 including retries (transport.rs:626-631, batch.rs:297), which is the exact shape that keeps the window open. The only test (`on_throttle_halves_once_per_window_and_floors_at_one`, :232-252) fires bursts at one instant then advances past the window, so it cannot observe it. Consequence is bounded (the per-request Retry-After handling still works) but a cap stuck at half under a storm burns retry budget and can turn into `unscored` → degraded runs. Proposal (separate `last_halved` from `last_throttle`) is small and correct.

    let _ = tx.unbounded_send(serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(raw).unwrap());

Note the upstream change also stops panicking on an undeserializable event (now `log::error!`, which no web-rs subscriber prints) — record that behaviour change next to the pin. Add a review date to the pin comment and, if desired, a `just deps-git-status` recipe (`git ls-remote` + commits ahead of the rev); the existing informal practice is the release-time check recorded in docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md:127.

Pinned checkout (~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tauri-sys-*/289bd29) has `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(raw).unwrap()` inside the listener Closure at src/event.rs:137 and :184, and in core.rs:14,25-26,126. A bare clone of upstream v2 shows exactly four commits after the pin; 1ffc6fa (2026-09-08, 'Update conversion of JsValues (#113)', bumps 0.2.4→0.2.5) adds lib.rs `from_value` that does `js_sys::JSON::stringify` + `serde_json::from_str` with the comment 'must serialize and deserialize to prevent overflowing wasm method table, see wasm-bindgen/issues/5324'. title: `invoke_result` unwraps the error deserialization — any rejection that is not a `UiError` JSON object panics the whole WASM app
evidence:
bindings/*.rs:  use tauri_sys::core::invoke_result;   (every binding, no wrapper)
tauri-sys/src/core.rs:18-27
  pub async fn invoke_result<T, E>(command: &str, args: impl Serialize) -> Result<T, E> {
      inner::invoke_result(command, swb::to_value(&args).unwrap())
          .await
          .map(|val| swb::from_value(val).unwrap())
          .map_err(|err| swb::from_value(err).unwrap())
.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:15  "use `invoke_result()` (never bare `invoke`, which panics on a rejected promise)"
rationale: The repo's rule treats `invoke_result` as the safe path, but tauri-sys `unwrap`s `from_value::<UiError>(err)`. Tauri rejects with a plain string (not `{code,message,retryable}`) for arg-shape mismatches ("invalid args `tenantId` for command …"), unknown commands, and denied plugin permissions (e.g. if `dialog:allow-save` is ever narrowed in capabilities/default.json). Any of those turns into a `console_error_panic_hook` panic (lib.rs:69) that freezes the UI with no toast — worse than the bare-`invoke` failure the rule warns about. Nothing pins binding arg names to backend param names today (`command-parity-check.sh` checks command names only), so this is one rename away.
proposal: Add `bindings::ipc::invoke_result<T: DeserializeOwned>(cmd, args) -> Result<T, UiError>` that calls `tauri_sys::core::invoke_result::<T, serde_json::Value>` and maps a value that fails `UiError` deserialization into `UiError::new("ipc", value.to_string(), false)` (also catching the success-side `from_value` failure). Mechanically switch every `use tauri_sys::core::invoke_result` in bindings/ to it, and add a repo_invariants source-scan test that bindings never import `tauri_sys::core::{invoke,invoke_result}` directly. Then `report_if_session_dead`/toasts see a real error instead of a panic.
verifier_notes: tauri-sys core.rs:18-27 (pinned rev 289bd29, Cargo.toml:33) does `.map(|val| swb::from_value(val).unwrap()).map_err(|err| swb::from_value(err).unwrap())`. `UiError` is a struct, so a string rejection (Tauri's shape for invalid-args deserialization failures and ACL/permission denials) fails `from_value` and panics; lib.rs:69 installs `console_error_panic_hook`, which logs and aborts the WASM instance with no toast. `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:15` presents `invoke_result` as the safe path, so the rule is misleading. Nothing pins binding arg names: repo_invariants/ has cache/cancel/commands/fanout/release/sources/trust only, and command-parity-check.sh compares command *names*. The GUI harness cannot catch this because `ipc_mock::mock_err` (ipc_mock/mod.rs:265-267) only ever rejects with a `UiError`. Proposal is feasible: deserialize both sides to `serde_json::Value` first and map failures to a synthetic `UiError`, plus a source-scan that bindings/ never import `tauri_sys::core::{invoke,invoke_result}` directly (note `defaults::get_tenant_defaults` and the diagnostics bindings use bare `invoke` by design as infallible commands — the wrapper should cover those too or leave them explicitly allow-listed).

title: `/` shortcut targets the first filter input in DOM order, so it no-ops once any earlier keep-alive pane has been visited

Either proposed fix (delta commands re-reading live like `upsert_api_scope`, or a `get_expose_api` immediately before computing the list) fits the repo's 'full-collection PATCH: re-read live, mutate, write back' convention.

title: Permissions tab consent/downgrade outcome notes are set right before `on_changed` unmounts the tab; consent failures never reach the operator
rationale: `bump_reload` re-runs the pane's `LocalResource`; the `Suspend` closure in application_detail_pane.rs:136-148 builds a fresh view (new `detail_signal`, new tab components) so every local signal in PermissionsTab is discarded. rationale: The client doc says "at or below" but ARM also returns assignments *above* the subscription (management groups, tenant root). A managed identity with Reader on a management group over 20 subscriptions appears 20 times in `list_managed_identity_azure_roles`, each row labelled with a different `subscription` display name, inflating the Azure RBAC footprint and the high-privilege count the operator sees. `readiness.rs` is unaffected (collects into a `HashSet` of GUIDs).

Add a unit test with two subscriptions returning the same MG-scoped assignment id and assert one row. Effort small; effect: no phantom duplicate roles.
