title: `atScope()` is documented as excluding inherited assignments; Azure defines it as "at or above the scope" — the Key Vault reverse lookup labels inherited subscription/RG roles as direct vault grants
rationale: The doc comment, the sweep's module doc, the DTO doc and two user-facing strings all assert the opposite of the documented ARM semantics. `atScope()` at a vault path returns the vault's own assignments PLUS every assignment inherited from its resource group, subscription, management group and root — the very "inherited subscription Owner" rows the comment says are excluded. The operator is told these are explicit vault grants and the panel's empty-state text claims inherited-only vaults "won't appear here", so the least-privilege picture is misreported (a subscription Owner is shown as a per-vault grant; a vault that is only reachable via inheritance shows rows anyway). `high_privilege` flags then fire on rows the user was told are direct.
proposal: Keep the `atScope()` query (it is the correct single call) but stop calling the rows direct: in `sweep_key_vault_access` compare `props.scope` to the vault `id` case-insensitively and either drop non-matching rows or add `inherited: bool` to `KeyVaultAccessRow` and render an "inherited from <scope level>" badge. Rewrite the doc comment at client.rs:90-94 to "at or above `scope`", fix keyvault_rbac.rs:5 / dto keyvault.rs:16 / the two UI strings (keyvault.rs:245, 354), and add a wiremock test in client.rs where one assignment's `scope` is the subscription and assert the consumer classifies it as inherited. Expected effect: the panel answers the question it claims to answer, and the "direct" label stops being wrong for every inherited Owner.
verifier_notes: Premise verified against Microsoft Learn (RoleAssignments list filter docs): '$filter=atScope() returns all role assignments at or above the scope' — i.e. it INCLUDES inherited assignments and excludes only child scopes. crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:90-94 asserts the opposite ('excludes assignments inherited from ancestor scopes'); the consumer keyvault_rbac.rs:266-268 does `props.scope.unwrap_or_else(|| vault_id.clone())` with no scope==vault comparison, so an RG/subscription/MG Owner is emitted as a row for every vault under it. Module doc keyvault_rbac.rs:5, DTO doc dto/keyvault.rs:16 ('One direct Azure-RBAC role assignment'), UI copy web-rs views/resource_access/keyvault.rs:245 and :354 all repeat the wrong semantics, and the panel table (keyvault.rs:365-410) has Vault/Principal/Role columns only — the row's real `scope` is never shown (only the CSV export carries it), so the operator cannot see provenance. The only test (client.rs:501-535) asserts the query param, not the semantics. Severity downgraded from high: the principals listed genuinely hold the role over the vault (inherited or not), so the access picture is complete and not false — what is wrong is the provenance labelling and the 'inherited-only vaults won't appear' claim. Proposal (keep atScope(), add `inherited: bool` by comparing `props.scope` to the vault id case-insensitively, render a badge, fix the five strings, add a wiremock test with a subscription-scoped `scope`) is sound and small.

title: Log Analytics `PartialError` responses (HTTP 200 + `error`) are treated as complete results — the granted-vs-used analysis can be built on truncated/failed query output
rationale: `usage.rs::get_app_graph_usage` turns the first table into `GraphUsageResult` and the UI uses it to recommend permission downgrades ("only GETs observed → Downgrade applies"). A runaway/timeout/truncation on a large 90-day `summarize` yields 200 with partial rows and an `error.code == "PartialError"`; the model discards `error`, so the panel shows fewer call patterns than exist and the operator may strip a permission the app actually uses. The DTO already models coverage honesty for `truncated` but has no channel for this case.
proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub error: Option<LogsErrorInfo { code: String, message: String }>` to `LogsQueryResponse`; in `LogAnalyticsClient::query` return `Err(ArmError::Protocol(format!("partial result: {code}: {message}")))` when `error` is present (or return `(table, partial: bool)` and thread a `partial` flag into `GraphUsageResult` beside `truncated` so the panel warns instead of failing). Add a wiremock test with `{"tables":[...],"error":{"code":"PartialError",...}}`. Effect: a degraded query can no longer read as an all-clear usage picture.
verifier_notes: Premise verified against Microsoft Learn 'Azure Monitor Log Analytics API response format': a non-fatal error returns 200 OK with `tables` plus an `error` property whose code is `PartialError`; the Kusto partial-query-failures page says the consumer should ignore the whole result. crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/models.rs:44-48 `LogsQueryResponse` has only `tables` (no `error`), loganalytics.rs:67-73 returns `tables[0]` unconditionally, and apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/usage.rs:257-267 builds `GraphUsageResult` with only `truncated` (dto/usage.rs:28-30) as its coverage-honesty channel. No handling anywhere (grep PartialError → none). This is the same class the repo pins elsewhere ('a cancelled/truncated/degraded run is never shown as all-clear', AGENTS.md). Severity lowered from high to medium: the trigger (runaway/truncation on a per-app 90-day summarize with `take 200`) is uncommon, and the Downgrade action is presented as admin-judged, not automatic. Proposal (add `error: Option<LogsErrorInfo>` with `#[serde(default)]`, surface as `ArmError::Protocol` or a `partial` flag beside `truncated`, wiremock test) is correct and small.

title: Tenant configured as a domain is accepted by the config screen but unconditionally rejected by sign_in
rationale: The id_token `tid` claim is always a GUID, so when the operator follows the UI's own guidance and enters `contoso.onmicrosoft.com` (accepted by `is_valid_tenant`, persisted to settings.json, used as the authority segment), every sign-in completes in the browser and then fails locally with 'id token tid ... does not match configured tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com'. `UserSettings::remembered_account_for` (settings.rs:171-175) does the same string compare, so restore would also never fire. No test exercises a domain-form tenant (tests use 't1'), and no code resolves a domain to its GUID (grep for well-known/openid-configuration only finds the SSO summary URL builder). README 384-401 tells users to copy the GUID, contradicting the config screen text.
proposal: Prefer (a): make `is_valid_tenant` GUID-only, align config.rs:44 and config_screen.rs:125/176-177 with README, and add a service/mod.rs test with a non-GUID configured tenant asserting the tid check. If domain support is wanted instead, resolve the domain to its GUID at sign_in time (GET `{auth_root}/{domain}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration`, issuer tid), compare `tid` to that, and persist the GUID so `remembered_account_for` matches — not in `AppState::new`, which is sync and runs before any network access.
verifier_notes: Premise holds. crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:313 does a plain string compare of the id_token `tid` (always a GUID) against `self.tenant_id`, which state.rs:241-258 sets verbatim from env/settings.json/bake with no domain→GUID resolution (state.rs:128-150 `resolve`). config.rs:41-46 + 71-72 accept a dotted domain and config_screen.rs:125/176-177 tell the operator a domain is fine, so a domain-configured install fails every sign-in after the browser round trip. settings.rs:171-175 `remembered_account_for` and state.rs:377 do the same string compare, so restore never fires either. No test uses a domain tenant (mod.rs:1029 uses 't1'; config.rs:80-87 only tests the validator). README.md:384-401 says GUID, contradicting the config screen. sign_in.rs:16-19 even documents that a wrong id 'comes back as an opaque token_exchange failure'. Severity lowered from high to medium: functional first-run bug with a clear workaround (enter the GUID) and an error message naming the mismatch, not a security or data-loss issue. Feasibility note on option (b): AppState::new is synchronous and offline, so resolving the domain there adds a blocking network call at launch; resolve lazily at sign_in instead.

title: sign_out clears in-memory session before the fallible keyring delete; on failure the restore pointer, data caches and refresh token survive while the UI reports 'still signed in'
rationale: If `delete_refresh_token` errors (locked Secret Service, Credential Manager hiccup, `ensure_keyring_store` failure), `sign_out` returns `Err` after `known_tenants` and the token cache were already cleared, and the command returns before `forget_account()` and `state.cache.invalidate_tenant(...)`. Result: (a) every subsequent command fails `not_signed_in` while the shell stays mounted and the toast says "you are still signed in" — false; (b) `settings.json.last_account` and the keyring refresh token both survive, so the NEXT launch `restore_session` revives the exact session the operator just tried to end — the fail-open direction on a shared workstation; (c) the tenant's data caches (`state.cache`) are not swept, contradicting the comment that sign-out "must" drop every tenant-scoped entry. The doc on `forget_account` says the two must not disagree about whether anyone is signed in; this path makes them disagree.
proposal: Make sign-out fail-safe: in `EntraAuthService::sign_out` attempt `delete_refresh_token` FIRST (via `spawn_blocking`, see the inline-keyring finding) and only then clear `cache`/`known_tenants`; in the command, run `forget_account()`, client removal and `state.cache.invalidate_tenant` unconditionally (before or regardless of the keyring result) and return the keyring error afterwards so the toast can say precisely "signed out, but the OS credential store still holds a token — remove the azapptoolkit entry manually". Update the shell.rs message accordingly. Add a service test with a keyring store that fails `delete_credential` (a small `keyring_core::CredentialStoreApi` fake) asserting `known_tenants` is empty AND the error is returned.
verifier_notes: Evidence real: service/mod.rs:561-566 invalidates the token cache and removes `known_tenants` BEFORE `delete_refresh_token(..)?`; commands/auth.rs:49 returns on Err before `forget_account()` (:53) and `state.cache.invalidate_tenant` (:61); shell.rs:82-85 tells the operator they are still signed in although every later command now fails `not_signed_in`. No repo_invariants test covers sign_out ordering. Downgraded from high: it needs a keyring failure at exactly that moment, the UI does tell the operator sign-out failed, and a retry re-runs the (idempotent) path; the fail-open next-launch restore only happens if the keyring later recovers. Still a real ordering bug worth the proposed fix (delete first, or clear pointer/caches unconditionally and report the keyring error afterwards).

title: CAE-ness is not part of the token cache key, and every interactive/restore flow seeds the Graph slots with non-CAE tokens — violating the invariant state.rs documents
rationale: `graph_for` (state.rs:417-464) builds every Graph adapter with `ScopedTokenAdapter::new_cae`, i.e. it expects `cp1`-advertised tokens in the `(tenant, scope_key)` slot. But `sign_in` (mod.rs:332), `consent_for_scopes` (381-388), `reauthenticate` (661-669), `refresh_session` (583) and `restore_session` (617) all put a token minted WITHOUT the `claims` parameter into those same slots. `authorize_url` (114-152) also sends no `claims`. So after launch (restore), after "Refresh Token", after every "Grant consent", and after reauth the Graph read/write adapters serve a non-CAE token for up to its full lifetime — exactly the class of bug the state.rs comment forbids for the `ensure_*` probes and that `readiness.rs:272-291` goes out of its way to avoid. CAE tokens are the ones that revoke promptly on password reset / disabled user / risky sign-in, which is the security property the app opted into.
proposal: Make it structural: include CAE-ness in the cache key (`TokenCache::get/put` take a `cae: bool` folded into `scope_key`, or a `CacheSlot { scopes, cae }`), so a non-CAE seed can never be served to a `new_cae` adapter — the worst case becomes one extra silent refresh. Then have the five flows mint CAE for Graph audiences: pass `claims = build_cae_claims(None)` on the `/authorize` and `/token` requests in `run_auth_code_flow` when the scope set is a Graph one, and use `access_token_for_scopes_cae(.., None)` in `refresh_session`/`restore_session`. Add a wiremock test asserting the `claims` form field is present on the refresh for a Graph scope set and that `cache.get(tenant, read_scopes, cae=true)` is what `graph_for` consumes.
verifier_notes: Evidence real. token_cache.rs:120-146 keys the cache by `(tenant_id, scope_key)` only; state.rs:417-469 builds every Graph adapter with `new_cae`, whose `bearer()` (token_adapter.rs:71-74) calls `access_token_for_scopes_cae(.., None)` → `access_token_inner` (mod.rs:478-483) returns whatever is in the slot. `sign_in` (mod.rs:332), `consent_for_scopes` (:381-388), `reauthenticate` (:661-668), `refresh_session` (:583) and `restore_session` (:617) all seed Graph scope slots with tokens minted without `claims` (`run_auth_code_flow` params :282-289 carry no `claims`; `authorize_url` :114-152 none either). state.rs:563-565 documents the invariant these flows violate; readiness.rs:277-283 honours it. No doc/CHANGELOG records this as deliberate (only CHANGELOG-archive.md:2530 mentions the CAE pairing). Impact is a lost security property (prompt revocation) for one token lifetime after each of those flows, not a functional break — medium is honest.

title: Group-membership token requests only GroupMember.ReadWrite.All; Learn documents that adding a servicePrincipal member also requires Application.ReadWrite.All
rationale: The member the app always adds is a service principal, which is exactly the row the docs single out. The dedicated token is minted from a single-scope request, so whether the resulting `scp` also carries `Application.ReadWrite.All` depends on the tenant having previously consented the write bundle for this client, not on anything the code asserts. The readiness checklist probes `consent_scopes_for("group_membership")` and reports the scope half as satisfied with only GroupMember consented, while the POST can still be rejected. Because outcomes vary with consent history, this is a latent 403 that the catalog cannot explain.
proposal: Change `default_graph_group_member_scopes` to `graph_scopes(&["GroupMember.ReadWrite.All", "Application.ReadWrite.All"])`, list both in the `group_membership` capability `scopes`, and mention the pair in its remediation string. Add a scopes.rs test mirroring `write_scopes_cover_mutations`.
verifier_notes: Learn 'Add members' permissions table (fetched) reads: servicePrincipal | GroupMember.ReadWrite.All and Application.ReadWrite.All | Not supported | GroupMember.ReadWrite.All and Application.ReadWrite.All. Repo requests only the first: crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/scopes.rs:79-81, minted into the dedicated adapter at state.rs:465-468 and used by `add_group_member`/`remove_group_member` (graph client/directory.rs:216-230). The catalog row lists only GroupMember (capabilities.rs:307) and the readiness scope probe uses `consent_scopes_for("group_membership")` (readiness.rs:58, 273 → state.rs:542), so the scope half reads 'have' with a scope set Learn says is insufficient for the only member type the app ever adds. Not documented as deliberate: docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:41 explains why not `Group.ReadWrite.All` but never addresses the SP-member pair. Caveat: Graph's runtime enforcement cannot be verified offline and the reviewer's 'depends on consent history' mechanism is speculative (v2 tokens carry only the requested scopes), but the remedy is the same either way and `Application.ReadWrite.All` is already in the write bundle (scopes.rs:150), so requesting it here widens nothing.

title: `interaction_required` / `login_required` are classified as a dead refresh token and purge the whole session; MSAL treats them as a per-resource step-up with the RT still valid
rationale: AADSTS50076/50079/50158 (MFA / registration / external challenge required by Conditional Access for THIS resource) come back from a `refresh_token` grant as `error: "interaction_required"`; AADSTS50074 similarly. The refresh token remains fully valid for other audiences — MSAL surfaces `InteractionRequiredAuthError` and re-acquires interactively for that resource without discarding the account. Here a first ARM/Exchange/Log Analytics call under a "Require MFA for Azure management" or authentication-strength policy deletes the keyring token, drops every cached access token and forgets the tenant, so Graph browsing dies too and the operator gets the `Re-authenticate` (`prompt=login`) toast. In the per-resource authentication-strength case the reauth mints only the Graph read token, the next ARM refresh fails again, and the purge repeats — a loop. The frontend's own hint table already treats these codes as "complete the MFA prompt", not "session dead", so the two layers disagree. error.rs:11-16 states the RT "must be discarded" for `interaction_required`; that premise is what this finding challenges.
proposal: Add `AuthError::InteractionRequired(String)` (UI code `interaction_required`, not in `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES`, `retryable=false`) for `interaction_required`/`login_required` and for `invalid_grant` whose AADSTS is 50074/50076/50079/50158; do NOT purge in `access_token_inner` for it (mirror the `ConsentRequired` arm). Recover with a scope-targeted interactive round trip: generalise `consent_for_scopes` into `interactive_for_scopes(tenant, scopes, prompt)` and expose a `request_scope_step_up(tenant_id, feature)` command (or reuse `request_scope_consent` with `prompt=login`), and teach `Session::report_command_error` to offer "Verify identity" on that code. Pin with wiremock tests: `interaction_required` keeps the keyring token and `known_tenants`; 70008 still purges.
verifier_notes: Evidence real: wire.rs:55-60 maps `interaction_required`/`login_required` to `InvalidGrant`, and mod.rs:529-538 purges the keyring token, all cached access tokens and the `known_tenants` entry. error.rs:14-16 documents the current stance ('must be discarded'), but Microsoft's own definition (MsalError.InteractionRequired: 'the application needs to expose the UI to the user so the user can do an interactive log-in to get a token with updated claims'; MSAL mitigation is AcquireTokenInteractive, the account is kept) contradicts it — the refresh token stays valid for other audiences. So a first ARM/Exchange/Log Analytics call under a resource-scoped MFA/authentication-strength CA policy kills Graph browsing too. The loop claim is real only when the policy is scoped to the non-Graph resource (a Graph `prompt=login` then does not satisfy it); with tenant-wide MFA one `reauthenticate` clears it — so the rationale slightly overstates frequency. sign_in.rs:225-228 already treats 50076/50079/50158 as 'complete MFA', confirming the layers disagree. Proposal (typed `InteractionRequired`, scope-targeted interactive step-up, no purge) is consistent with the existing `ConsentRequired` arm.

title: Rule 13 emits the broad-prefix delegated advisory for declared scopes regardless of consent; the group blurb and predicate doc promise admin-consented ones
rationale: For an app-registration row `scope_values` is the manifest's declared delegated scopes, and `rule_high_risk_delegated` never consults `perms.has_admin_consent`. Since the rule was widened to the broad-prefix predicate (`Mail.`, `Files.`, `Group.`, `Sites.`, `Directory.`…), every app that merely declares a user-consent `Mail.Read` or `Files.Read` delegated scope now lands in the "High-risk delegated permissions" group whose blurb says "Admin-consented delegated scopes". Delegated access under user consent is confined to the consenting user, so the group misleads the operator and buries the genuinely admin-consented cases. The only Rule 13 test (tests.rs:394-415) exercises just the two exact entries plus `User.Read`, so the broad-prefix behaviour under `score_application` is unpinned.
proposal: Thread the per-client AllPrincipals scope set the runner already keeps (audit.rs:914-931, `delegated_scopes_by_client`) into app rows too, so the rule can tell an admin-consented scope from a merely declared, user-consentable one; keep the two PS entries unconditional; emit the broad-prefix half only for consented scopes, or word it separately ("declared" vs "admin-consented"). Do NOT gate on the coarse `has_admin_consent` flag alone: the grants read is best-effort (audit.rs:933-939) and a failed read would silently hide the advisory, against the over-report-is-safe stance at permissions.rs:194-197. Fix groups.rs:113 to match whatever the rule actually reports, and add the table rows.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: scoring.rs:480-484 filters `perms.scope_values` with `is_risky_delegated_scope` and never reads `has_admin_consent`; for app rows `scope_values` is the declared manifest (audit.rs:1475); permissions.rs:167-169 says "when admin-consented"; groups.rs:113 blurb says "Admin-consented delegated scopes"; the widening comment at scoring.rs:471-479 and CHANGELOG-archive:377-381 frame the change around admin-consented scopes; the only Rule-13 table (tests.rs:399-403) has three rows. Overstated: for SP rows `scope_values` IS the AllPrincipals grant set (audit.rs:1264-1267), so the blurb is right there; and the proposed `has_admin_consent` gate is app-level, not per-scope, and fails silent when the tenant-wide grants read fails. Advisory only (no score), so medium is for group noise/mislabeling, not ranking.

title: rewrite_identifier_uris only rewrites the exact `api://{appId}` form; `api://{tenantId}/{appId}`, `api://{string}/{appId}` and `api://{tenantId}/...` fail the Expose-an-API PATCH on restore
rationale: `api://{tenantId}/{appId}` is one of Microsoft's two 'default' identifier URIs (the only two allowed once an org enables `nonDefaultUriAddition`), and `api://{string}/{appId}` is a common alternative. Both keep the SOURCE appId (and, cross-tenant, the SOURCE tenant GUID), which the destination tenant rejects because the GUID matches neither the new appId nor the destination tenant. The failure is not isolated: the identifier URIs share one PATCH with `oauth2PermissionScopes` and `preAuthorizedApplications`, so the app's whole Expose-an-API surface is lost with a single warning line. The backup carries `source_tenant_id` and the restore knows the destination tenant, so a correct rewrite is possible.
proposal: Change the helper to `rewrite_identifier_uris(uris, source_app_id, new_app_id, source_tenant_id, dest_tenant_id)` and rewrite every `api://` URI whose host or path segment equals `source_app_id` → `new_app_id` or equals `source_tenant_id` → `dest_tenant_id` (segment-wise, case-insensitive GUID compare; leave `https://` and verified-domain forms untouched). Add table tests for `api://{tenant}/{app}`, `api://{tenant}/api`, `api://productapi/{app}`, and a substring non-match. Update docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:148 ("`api://{old}` → `api://{new}`"). Effect: cross-tenant restores keep their Expose-an-API configuration instead of dropping URIs, scopes and pre-authorized clients together.
verifier_notes: The helper is at restore_plan.rs:50-61 (not :176, which is inside the tests) and matches only the exact `api://{source_app_id}` string. restore.rs:419-437 puts the rewritten URIs, `oauth2PermissionScopes` and `preAuthorizedApplications` in ONE `patch_application_expose_api` call, so a rejected URI drops the whole Expose-an-API surface with a single warning. Microsoft's identifier-URI restrictions page lists `api://<tenantId>/<appId>`, `api://<tenantId>/<string>`, `api://<string>/<appId>` as supported forms and says a GUID 'must match either the app ID or the tenant ID'; the `nonDefaultUriAddition` policy allows only `api://{appId}` or `api://{tenantId}/{appId}`. The reviewer did not cite the deliberate-decision comment at restore_plan.rs:151-154 ('the appId form is the ONLY one that encodes an identity the restore invalidates'), but that rationale is factually incomplete - `api://{tenantId}/{appId}` encodes both identities the restore changes - so it does not refute the finding. `TenantBackup.source_tenant_id` (dto/backup.rs:48) and `destination_tenant_id` (restore.rs:136-138) are available. Proposal is feasible; note the tenant segment rewrite is a no-op on same-tenant restores and GUID comparison should be case-insensitive. docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:148 needs the wording update.

title: Mailbox advisory and scope gate omit the newer RBAC-scopable Graph mailbox permissions (MailboxItem.*, MailboxFolder.*, Mail-Advanced.*) — a documented but audit-relevant gap

Add `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All`, `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All` to HIGH_RISK and the read variants to MEDIUM_RISK in audit/permissions.rs with the CHANGELOG note exchange-scoping.md:48-49 already requires; keep `aap.rs` on the 11-value AAP set (it is the migration parity contract) and update exchange-scoping.md:46-50.

title: UserSettings::mutate overwrites an unparseable or unreadable settings.json with defaults — vault bindings and tenant defaults are permanently lost
rationale: The atomic temp-and-rename closed the *torn write* cause of an unparseable file, but `mutate` still treats "file exists but cannot be parsed" and "file exists but cannot be read (EACCES, EIO, AV lock on Windows)" identically to "file missing", then serialises defaults over it. Any of: a hand-edit typo (which defaults.rs explicitly expects), a future field type change, or a transient read failure, followed by the very next `mutate` (sign-in calls `remember_account` via `mutate` on every successful login) wipes `tenant_defaults` including `app_vaults` — the map the rotation flow needs to find secrets again — and the only trace is a `warn!` in the log. Data loss with no recovery.
proposal: Make `from_file` return `Result<Option<Self>, io::Error>` distinguishing `ErrorKind::NotFound` (→ `Ok(None)`) from parse/IO failures. Keep `stored()`'s lenient fallback for read-only callers, but have `mutate` refuse (`Err(InvalidData)`) when the file exists and cannot be parsed — or first rename it to `settings.json.corrupt-<timestamp>` and log at `error!` before writing defaults. Callers already treat `mutate` errors as non-fatal (state.rs:347-355, keyvault.rs:167-171). Add a test: write `not json`, call `mutate`, assert the original bytes (or a `.corrupt` sibling) survive.
verifier_notes: Evidence is exact. `mutate` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:121-123) starts from `Self::stored`, which is `from_file(..).unwrap_or_default()` (75-77), and `from_file` (223-232) collapses both an I/O error (`std::fs::read(path).ok()?` — EACCES/EIO/AV lock) and a parse error into `None` with only a `warn!`. `save_locked` then serialises the defaults over the file. private_file.rs:39-41 documents this exact loss mechanism but only closed the torn-write cause; defaults.rs:125-126 explicitly anticipates hand-edited settings.json. `remember_account` (state.rs:345-355) runs `mutate` on every successful sign-in, so the overwrite happens promptly. No `.bak`/`.corrupt` sibling or recovery exists (grep). No test covers 'unparseable file survives a mutate'. One nuance on the proposal: only two of the four writer files treat a `mutate` error as non-fatal (state.rs:347-355 warn, keyvault.rs:167-171 push a warning); config.rs:52-57 and defaults.rs:72-75 return `UiError::io('Could not write settings.json: ...')` to the operator — which is the desirable behaviour for a refused write, so the proposal still fits. Medium is honest: silent, permanent loss of `app_vaults`/tenant defaults, but requires a prior corruption/read failure.

title: Tenant-wide list reads that gate the irreversible group delete use invoke_optional, so a misclassified 400 reads as 'no references'
rationale: invoke_optional exists so an `-Identity` that does not resolve reads as None. An identity-less `Get-ManagementScope`/`Get-ApplicationAccessPolicy` has no object to be missing: an empty tenant returns 200 with `value: []`. Routing them through invoke_optional means any 400 whose sanitized body happens to contain "not found"/"couldn't be found" (a parameter set that cannot be resolved, a cmdlet the caller's role does not expose, an EXO wording change) becomes `Ok(vec![])`. `retired_scope_groups` then reports `reference_check_complete: true` and `delete_exchange_scope_group` re-checks live through the same path and finds zero references - exactly the 'unknown read as clean' the docs say must never happen. `list_service_principals` (rbac.rs:59-64) already uses invoke_command, so the two list-alls are also inconsistent with their sibling.
proposal: Switch `list_management_scopes` and `get_application_access_policies` to `invoke_command` (keep `get_management_scope`/`get_service_principal`/`get_group`, which take an Identity, on invoke_optional). Add a wiremock test: `Get-ManagementScope` with `{}` returning 400 "...not found..." must be `Err(ExchangeError::Api{..})`, not `Ok(vec![])`. Optionally tighten `is_not_found_body` to require the cmdlet-shaped phrasings ("couldn't be found", "ManagementObjectNotFound") and drop the bare "not found".
verifier_notes: rbac.rs:220-225 and :270-275 route the identity-less list-alls through invoke_optional; transport.rs:144 maps any `Api` whose body passes is_not_found_body to Ok(vec![]), and error.rs:158 matches bare 'not found'. list_service_principals (rbac.rs:59-64) uses invoke_command, so the siblings are inconsistent. scope_group.rs:354 `readable = scopes.is_ok() && policies.is_ok()` and :438-443 treat an Ok(empty) as 'no references' before an irreversible Remove-DistributionGroup (:457). Introduced in 0389543 with no rationale comment; references.rs:11-17 explicitly says an unknown must never read as clean. The trigger (a 4xx with 'not found' text on an identity-less list) is hypothetical, but the fix is one line per call site and the consequence is irreversible, so medium is fair.

title: Mid-pagination errors are flattened to Protocol, losing auth/throttle classification and the re-auth-fatal signal
rationale: The comment justifies the reclassification only for NotFound (so invoke_optional cannot read a 404 on page 2 as an empty collection), but the arm catches every error. A `Token` error carrying `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` from the bearer() call on page 2 becomes `protocol_error`, so `is_reauth_fatal` is false and a long-running fan-out (the audit's Exchange probes, bulk remediations) keeps going on a dead session, contrary to the AGENTS.md invariant that every long-running loop stops on a re-auth-fatal code. Likewise a 401/403/429 on page 2 no longer matches the audit's Exchange breaker or ui_hint branches; the operator sees a generic protocol error instead of the stale-token guidance.
proposal: Narrow the arm: reclassify to Protocol only `ExchangeError::NotFound(_)` and `ExchangeError::Api { body, .. } if is_not_found_body(&body)`; return every other error unchanged (they already prevent a truncated Ok). Add two wiremock tests: page-2 401 -> `ExchangeError::Unauthorized`; page-2 StaticTokenProvider failure with code refresh_missing -> `ui_code() == "refresh_missing"`.

The only pinned test (client/tests.rs:709) covers the 404 case. Proposal is correct and minimal.

title: Exchange transport replays non-idempotent cmdlets (New-/Remove-) on 5xx and network errors
rationale: Commit 8fb1ac7 ("stop replaying writes") added RetryReason/RetryClass to with_retries so a POST that hit a connection reset or 502 after the server committed is not replayed; Graph, ARM and Key Vault all route through with_retries + retry_class_for. The Exchange transport never used with_retries (it open-codes attempt/delay_ms/MAX_RETRIES), so it escaped both the fix and the repo invariant `every_retry_call_site_derives_its_idempotency_class` (trust.rs:160: files without `with_retries(` are skipped). Every cmdlet here is a POST, and the crate's own writes are not replay-safe: a replayed `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:232-246) after a committed write fails as a duplicate, which grants.rs:118 records as `failed to assign` -> role_in_place=false -> targets_safe_to_strip keeps the org-wide grant, so the scope silently has no effect (the exact failure mode RoleStep::SameRoleAs was added to prevent). A replayed `Remove-ApplicationAccessPolicy` (rbac.rs:277-284) after a committed delete returns a not-found 400, which aap_migration.rs:371-376 reports as `failed to remove legacy policy` and status `partial` while the policy is actually gone. `New-ServicePrincipal`, `New-ManagementScope`, `New-DistributionGroup`, `Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment` and `Remove-DistributionGroup` have the same exposure.
proposal: Same as proposed, with one adjustment: name the helper `retry_class_for(` (taking the cmdlet name), not `retry_class_for_cmdlet(` — trust.rs:167 matches the literal `retry_class_for(`, so once transport.rs contains `with_retries(` the differently named helper would make the crate an offender. Extend the trust.rs invariant so a crate whose transport calls `.send()` without `with_retries(` is flagged instead of skipped.
verifier_notes: Premise verified. transport.rs:168-190 retries a reqwest send error and :263-271 retries every 429/5xx unconditionally, for every cmdlet (all POSTs). `git log -S with_retries -- crates/azapptoolkit-exchange` is empty: the exchange transport never adopted `with_retries`/`RetryClass`; 8fb1ac7 touched transport.rs only for the nextLink same-origin check. trust.rs:163 skips any file without `with_retries(`, so the invariant is silently vacuous for this crate, while http_retry.rs:1-3 claims Exchange is among the unified clients. Consequence chain checks out: grants.rs:118 `failed to assign` -> role_in_place=false -> targets_safe_to_strip keeps the org-wide grant; aap_migration.rs:371-376 reports `partial`. Severity downgraded from high: Exchange objects are name-keyed, so a replayed New-*/Remove-* fails as duplicate/not-found rather than double-committing (no analog of the orphaned-secret outcome that motivated 8fb1ac7); the result is a false failure that is reported (grants.rs:286 warns 'scoping is NOT effective') and self-heals on re-run via RoleStep::AlreadyScoped (rbac.rs / targets.rs plan). Still a real invariant gap worth fixing. Membership mutators are already idempotent (groups.rs:77-108 swallow already-/not-a-member), so classing them Idempotent is right.

title: Exchange transport open-codes the retry loop with no RetryClass, so New-/Remove- cmdlets are replayed after transient failures and misreport a committed write as a failure; the hand-rolled loop escapes the trust.rs invariant
rationale: Every Exchange admin call is a POST to InvokeCommand, and `send_core` retries a connection reset or 5xx up to MAX_RETRIES times regardless of the cmdlet. A `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` that committed server-side before a 502 is re-run and creates a second, identical role assignment; a later `Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment` by identity removes one and the app keeps its mailbox access — the operator sees "removed" while access persists. `New-ServicePrincipal`/`New-ManagementScope` replays surface as "already exists" failures after a successful write. This is exactly the class `RetryClass::NonIdempotent` closed for Graph/ARM/Key Vault, but the `trust.rs` invariant scans only `with_retries(` call sites, so the hand-rolled Exchange loop is invisible to it. http_retry.rs's own header ("Shared retry policy for the Graph, ARM, Key Vault and Exchange HTTP clients") and the `with_retries` doc ("The four HTTP clients each open-coded this loop", past tense) both state a unification that has not happened for Exchange.
proposal: Port `send_core` onto `with_retries(label, class, |_| ...)` with a `retry_class_for(cmdlet)` helper: `Get-`/`Test-`/`Search-` and paging continuations → Idempotent; `New-`/`Remove-`/`Set-`/`Update-` → NonIdempotent (`Add-DistributionGroupMember` may stay Idempotent since `is_already_member_body` already makes a re-add benign). Keep the `x-ms-diagnostics`/`request-id` capture inside the per-attempt closure. Extend `repo_invariants/trust.rs` so any crate source outside `http_retry.rs` that references `MAX_RETRIES`, `next_backoff_ms` or `sleep_before_retry` directly (rather than via `with_retries`/`RetryBudget`) fails the test. Add a wiremock test that a `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` answered 502 is NOT re-sent and a `Get-*` answered 502 IS. Fix the http_retry.rs:160-165 doc that presents the four-client unification as complete. Drop the 'duplicate assignment survives removal' framing — grants.rs:74-78 and 459-468 show Exchange rejects the duplicate and removal sweeps every assignment.
verifier_notes: The mechanism is real: crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/transport.rs:11-14 imports only the raw primitives, and `send_core` retries every POST on a reqwest error (181-188) and on 429/5xx (265-270) up to `MAX_RETRIES` with no `RetryClass`; `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:243), `New-ServicePrincipal` (rbac.rs:31), `New-ManagementScope` (rbac.rs:80), `Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:260) all ride it. The `trust.rs` invariant (apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/trust.rs:163) skips any file without `with_retries(`, so the loop is invisible to it; commit 8fb1ac7 (the RetryClass fix) touched transport.rs only for the same-origin check, and its CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:504-515) claims 'the transports route everything through it'. No Exchange test covers a 5xx/network replay (only `retry_after_is_honored_on_429`, tests.rs:492). This is a genuine gap against AGENTS.md's 'one definition per policy' rule. But the headline harm is refuted by the repo's own code: (a) a duplicate `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` for the same role/app/scope FAILS on Exchange rather than creating a second assignment — grants.rs:74-78 records exactly that ('every duplicate `New-RoleAssignment` failed'); (b) `remove_exchange_mailbox_access` (grants.rs:459-468) enumerates every assignment via `Get-ManagementRoleAssignment -RoleAssignee` and removes each, so even a duplicate would not leave access behind; (c) `assign_scoped_roles` (grants.rs:92-93) plans against the live snapshot, so a replay-induced 'failed to assign' leaves `role_in_place = false` and `targets_safe_to_strip` keeps the org-wide grant — fail-closed, healed on re-run; (d) `ensure_management_scope`/`ensure_service_principal` re-read before creating, and `Add-DistributionGroupMember` already treats 'already a member' as success (error.rs:166, tests.rs:412). So the realistic consequence is a misreported outcome (a committed write replayed surfaces as 'failed to assign' / 'failed to remove') and a wasted re-run, not widened or persisting access. Medium, not high.

title: DN set comparisons are case-sensitive in the consolidation path but case-folded in the post-write proof, so a landed repoint can be reported as a mismatch
evidence:
repoint: !(source_dns.len() == 1 && source_dns[0] == managed_dn),
-- targets.rs:480-486 (same file): "Exchange Online normalises the casing of the DNs it returns ... a case-sensitive HashSet comparison of 'what I wrote' against 'what the server reports' can differ on a write that DID land." rbac.rs:197 `if wanted_groups.folded_dns() != landed.folded_dns()`; but scope_group.rs:540 `g.complete && g.dns == group_dns_in_filter(wanted)` and scope_group.rs:744 `&& source_dns[0] == dn`.

Extend `consolidation_is_a_no_op_when_the_scope_is_already_managed` with a case-variant DN. Consider `to_lowercase()` instead of `to_ascii_lowercase()` in `folded_dns` so a `CN=Zürich…` DN folds too.

In every case one side is a DN parsed from Exchange's echoed RecipientFilter and the other a DN from a group object (grants.rs:162, aap_migration.rs:200, scope_group.rs:742), which is exactly the pair targets.rs:480-486 says can differ. Consequence (1) is real: reconcile_scope_filter (scope_group.rs:575-619) would issue a redundant repoint, pass rbac.rs's folded proof, then fail `scope_filter_agrees(f, wanted)` at :612 with scope_filter_mismatch, blocking a correct migration. Failure direction is safe (refusal/redundant write, never widening), and the trigger rests on the crate's own claim about Exchange casing rather than a pinned observation, so medium rather than high. The existing test at targets.rs:1353 uses identical casing and would not catch it.

title: Claims-mapping policy assign/list ride a Policy-only token; Learn requires Application.ReadWrite.All AND a Policy.* scope
rationale: Creating the policy (`POST /policies/claimsMappingPolicies`) genuinely needs only `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration`, but the two `$ref` operations on the service principal are documented as needing `Application.ReadWrite.All` in the same token. As with the group-member token, success today depends on Entra folding previously consented write scopes into a single-scope request. Listing assigned policies is also a read that could ride `Policy.Read.All` + `Application.ReadWrite.All` rather than forcing the admin-consent-only write scope on a read path.

Document the pair in a new capability entry (see the catalog-gap finding).

Repo: crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs:26-58 and :62-74 ride `policy_write_token`, minted with the single scope at scopes.rs:55-57 / state.rs:449-452, so the `$ref` assign/list/remove calls carry no `Application.ReadWrite.All`. The browse path `get_sso_config` (sso/mod.rs:455-470) calls the list on every SSO-tab open and only degrades. title: assign_managed_identity_azure_role never busts the Key Vault access sweep cache
rationale: The sweep result is cached for the 60-minute Audit TTL and is the answer to "who can touch this vault?". A role assigned by this very app at a `/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/...` scope changes that answer, but `get_cached_key_vault_access` keeps serving the pre-assignment sweep until TTL — contradicting the repo's invalidate-on-Ok rule and the sweep's own "coverage is never overstated" stance.
proposal: Make `kv_sweep_cache_key` `pub(crate)` (keyvault_rbac.rs:55) and, on the `Ok` path of `assign_managed_identity_azure_role` (managed_identity.rs:389-419), invalidate `CacheKind::Audit` / `kv_sweep_cache_key(&tenant_id)` unconditionally rather than only when the scope string contains a vault path: the sweep's rows keep `props.scope` (keyvault_rbac.rs:268) from an `atScope()` query, and per Microsoft's Role Assignments docs `atScope()` returns assignments at or above the scope, so an RG- or subscription-level assignment also changes the vault answer. The key is one per tenant and only re-filled by an explicit sweep, so an unconditional bust costs nothing. Add the pairing to repo_invariants/cache.rs.
verifier_notes: Premise confirmed: `assign_managed_identity_azure_role` ends with `Ok(())` and no cache call; `kv_sweep_cache_key` is private and referenced only in keyvault_rbac.rs (:55, :320, :368, :480); no repo_invariants file mentions the command or the key; the frontend lets an operator type any `/subscriptions/...` scope (managed_identity_detail_pane.rs:538). The sweep result is cached for the Audit TTL (keyvault_rbac.rs:320) and `get_cached_key_vault_access` serves it (:358-370), so the pre-assignment answer is served until TTL — contradicting invalidate-on-Ok. Overstated part: the vault-path-only condition is too narrow given the sweep retains inherited scopes (and the ARM client's own comment at client.rs:90-94 that atScope() excludes ancestors disagrees with Microsoft's documentation). Low is fair.

title: `save_backup_to_file` / `save_restore_report_to_file` write `{}` on a serialization failure instead of erroring
evidence:
restore.rs:354 `|| serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string()),`
backup.rs:295 `|| serde_json::to_string_pretty(&backup).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string()),`
restore.rs:337-341 doc: "**The report contains the regenerated client-secret values** (show-once) ... the UI warns the operator to store it securely"
rationale: Serialization of these plain structs is practically infallible today, but the failure direction is wrong: the report is the ONLY place the show-once secrets exist, and this path would silently write an empty object and return the chosen path as success. A future field (e.g. a map with non-string keys) would turn this into silent data loss.
proposal: Make `save_export_via_dialog`'s `to_json` closure return `Result<String, UiError>` (or serialize before calling it) and map the error to `UiError::serde(...)`; apply to both call sites. Effort S.
verifier_notes: Both sites verified: restore.rs:354 and backup.rs:295 pass `|| serde_json::to_string_pretty(&x).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string())` as `to_json`, and `save_export_via_dialog` (export.rs:39-61) then writes whatever string it gets and returns the path as success. The restore report is documented as the only home of the show-once secrets (restore.rs:337-341), so the failure direction is wrong even though serialization of these plain structs cannot realistically fail today. `UiError::serde` already exists (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:103). Scoping note for the fix: `save_export_via_dialog` has eight callers (enterprise_application.rs:553, sharepoint.rs:1072, backup.rs:290, managed_identity.rs:471, permission_tester.rs:1188, restore.rs:349, keyvault_rbac.rs:392, applications/mod.rs:461), so the least invasive change is to serialize before the call and `?` the error at the two DR sites rather than changing the closure signature for all eight.

title: Restore regenerates a live secret for every backed-up password credential, including ones already expired at backup time
rationale: Long-lived app registrations commonly carry several expired secrets nobody rotated away. Restore turns each of them into a fresh, valid credential whose plaintext lands in the report — widening the destination tenant's credential surface beyond what was actually in use, and inflating the redistribution work. The metadata needed to distinguish them is already in the manifest.
proposal: Skip secrets whose `end_date_time` is earlier than `backup.created_at` (TenantBackup.created_at, dto/backup.rs:44) — not `Utc::now()`: a secret that was live when the manifest was taken but expired since is exactly the one a DR client still holds and needs re-issued. Push a per-app warning naming the skipped secret and its source expiry, have `build_restore_plan` count only non-expired-at-backup secrets plus an `expired_secrets_skipped` count, and rewrite the comment at restore.rs:78-81 to state the rule. Unit-test both branches.
verifier_notes: Premise true: restore.rs:588-598 iterates every `app.secrets` entry with no expiry filter, backup.rs:461 captures all password credentials, and `CredentialMeta.end_date_time` (dto/backup.rs:263) is available. However the reviewer did not engage with restore.rs:78-81, which explicitly acknowledges 'the original expiry ... may be in the past' and chooses to mint a fresh window anyway — a documented decision, though its rationale is thin (a secret expired before the backup cannot have been in use). The proposal's `Utc::now()` cutoff is wrong for DR: it would drop secrets that were live at backup and expired during the outage. Severity lowered to low: the report is already handled as secret-bearing (restore.rs:337-341), and the exposure is orphaned live credentials (hygiene the app's own audit flags), not disclosure.

title: global_search (and prefetch_search_corpus / get_directory_index_status) answer from cache without proving the session, and the invariant that pins the rule cannot see them
rationale: session.rs documents that a read-through command whose hit path returns before a token is fetched must call `prove_tenant_session` first, because otherwise the `tenant_id` argument alone decides whose directory data is returned (tenant switch mid-flight; dead session with data caches kept). `graph_for` only constructs token adapters (no token is acquired until a request), so on a warm corpus `global_search` returns the previous session's app/SP names having proven nothing. The invariant passes vacuously: the `cache.get_typed` lives inside `search_corpus`, not the command body, and `graph_for(` is accepted as a proof. `prefetch_search_corpus` (search.rs:235-236) and `get_directory_index_status` (mod.rs:108-109, via `sp_index_cached`) have the same shape, with less to leak. Sign-out sweeps the caches, so the exposure is the mid-flight switch and dead-session cases, which is why this is medium rather than high.
proposal: Add `crate::commands::session::prove_tenant_session(&state, &tenant_id)?;` as the first statement of `global_search`, `prefetch_search_corpus` and `get_directory_index_status`. Harden the invariant: extend `first_cache_read` to also match the cached-accessor names (`sp_index_cached(`, `app_name_index_cached(`, `indexes_cached(`, `search_corpus(`, `sp_index_hit(`, `load_gallery_corpus(`), and drop `graph_for(`/`*_for(` from `SESSION_PROOFS` (a factory call is not a proof); bump `KNOWN_CACHE_READING_COMMANDS` accordingly.
verifier_notes: Premise holds: search.rs:254 builds the client via `graph_for` (state.rs:415-440 only constructs `ScopedTokenAdapter`s — token_adapter.rs:54-65 is a plain struct build, no token acquired), and search.rs:302 / :235-236 / applications/mod.rs:108-109 answer from `get_typed` inside helpers (search.rs:114-118, cache.rs:234-236), which repo_invariants/cache.rs `first_cache_read` (scans only `cmd.body`, sources.rs:138-178) cannot see; `graph_for(` is in SESSION_PROOFS at cache.rs:564-571. The repo's own commands already say `graph_for` on the miss path is not a proof (mod.rs:134-136, :231-233; credentials.rs:41-44). The dead-session exposure is real: auth service/mod.rs:537 and :624 purge `known_tenants` on RefreshTokenMissing while data caches are kept, so `tenant_context` is None yet a warm corpus is served. Severity lowered to low: sign_out sweeps the tenant cache (service/mod.rs:561-566), so the data returned always belongs to a tenant this same process/operator signed into; the practical effect is search keeps answering from cache instead of raising `not_signed_in` to trigger in-place re-auth. Proposal note: dropping `graph_for(` from SESSION_PROOFS also catches keyvault_rbac.rs:106/:227 (`graph_for` before a per-item `cache.get` inside a closure), which would need a `prove_tenant_session` too — cheap and correct.

title: Log (and config) directory is created with the process umask while every file the app writes is owner-only
rationale: The rolling logs carry tenant ids, the signed-in scope set, authorize endpoint, app display names (audit.rs:1497), correlation ids, Graph error bodies (see previous finding) and panic backtraces, and settings.json was made 0600 for a weaker class of content ('config-sensitive'). `tracing_appender` creates files with default 0644 under whatever mode `create_dir_all` gives the directory, so on a shared Linux/macOS workstation with a 755 home the 14 days of logs are world-readable.
proposal: On unix create both `log_directory()` and `config_directory()` with `DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700)` and `set_permissions(0o700)` afterwards to tighten an existing directory; document the Windows ACL inheritance as private_file.rs does, and add a one-line note to DEVELOPMENT.md's security model.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: lib.rs:339-340 `create_dir_all(&log_dir)` (and lib.rs:32 for the config dir) leave the mode to the umask, while private_file.rs:12-16/71-75 makes settings.json and exports 0600 with an explicit rationale. Overstated: on macOS `~/Library` is 0700 by default, so `~/Library/Application Support/azapptoolkit/logs` is already owner-only there; on Linux many distros now create homes 0750 (Ubuntu >= 21.04), so exposure is limited to 755-home setups. tracing_appender files remain 0644, but a 0700 directory is sufficient. No doc or test covers log-directory permissions. Severity low holds.

title: Webview grants wider than used: connect-src external hosts and updater/dialog capabilities are backend-only concerns
evidence:
tauri.conf.json:25 `"csp": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' https://graph.microsoft.com https://graph.microsoft.us ... https://login.microsoftonline.com ... https://*.vault.azure.net ... https://management.azure.com ..."`
capabilities/default.json:6-12 `"permissions": ["core:default", "core:window:default", "core:app:default", "updater:default", "dialog:allow-save"]`
AGENTS.md: "**CSP governs the webview only** — backend reqwest egress needs no `connect-src` change."
web-rs/Cargo.toml has no HTTP client (only `web-sys` features for DOM/clipboard/storage); grep of web-rs/src for `plugin:` finds only `plugin:event|listen` in ipc_mock; all updater/dialog work is backend-side (`commands::updater`, `export::write_bytes_via_dialog`).
backup.rs:301-306 `load_backup_from_file` uses `.blocking_pick_file()` with NO `dialog:allow-open` capability — proving backend dialogs need no webview grant.
rationale: All network egress is backend reqwest; the WASM frontend only invokes custom commands and listens to events. The `connect-src` allowlist therefore protects nothing and, should the webview ever be compromised, permits it to reach Graph/login endpoints directly. `updater:default` grants `plugin:updater|check/download/install/download_and_install` to the webview, and `dialog:allow-save` grants a save dialog, neither of which the frontend uses — the backend already drives both via Rust APIs (the `pick_file` path works without any dialog grant). Least privilege says drop them.
proposal: Remove `updater:default` and `dialog:allow-save` (and the redundant `core:window:default`/`core:app:default`) from capabilities/default.json, then run the export/updater GUI shards. Separately tighten `connect-src`: Tauri's `set_csp` (tauri-2.11.6/src/manager/mod.rs:53-106) only rewrites script-src/style-src hashes and does not append IPC origins, and the tauri-utils example (config.rs:2741) writes `connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost` explicitly — so confirm with `just dev` on each OS that invokes still flow with `'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost`, and pin the final directive in a repo_invariants test so it cannot regrow. Update the AGENTS.md CSP sentence.
verifier_notes: Premise is accurate: web-rs has no HTTP client (apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml deps are leptos/thaw/tauri-sys core+event/web-sys), the only `plugin:` strings are `plugin:event|*` in ipc_mock/mod.rs:125-146, all updater work is in commands/updater.rs and all dialogs go through the Rust API (export.rs `write_bytes_via_dialog`, backup.rs:305-310 `pick_file` with no `dialog:allow-open` grant — proof capabilities do not gate the Rust side). No test or doc pins the CSP or capabilities (grep of tests/, docs/architecture, AGENTS.md). Overstated on risk: tokens never reach the webview and updater payloads are signature-verified (README.md:250-253), so a compromised webview gains little from either the hosts or the grants — this is least-privilege hygiene, hence low. The CSP replacement value needs the verification step the reviewer already includes.

tauri.conf.json:25:
"csp": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' https://graph.microsoft.com https://graph.microsoft.us https://dod-graph.microsoft.us https://microsoftgraph.chinacloudapi.cn https://login.microsoftonline.com https://login.microsoftonline.us https://login.partner.microsoftonline.cn https://*.vault.azure.net https://*.vault.usgovcloudapi.net https://*.vault.azure.cn https://management.azure.com https://management.usgovcloudapi.net https://management.chinacloudapi.cn; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'"

The fact that the list omits the Exchange and Log Analytics hosts (which the backend does call) without anything breaking is direct proof nothing in the webview depends on it, and also shows there is no test tying it to `CloudEnvironment`.

If a webview-side fetch is ever added, re-derive the list from `CloudEnvironment` and pin it with a repo_invariants test. title: CSP connect-src allowlists 13 Microsoft origins the WASM frontend never contacts, contrary to the repo's own CSP rule
evidence:
tauri.conf.json:25:
"csp": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' https://graph.microsoft.com https://graph.microsoft.us https://dod-graph.microsoft.us https://microsoftgraph.chinacloudapi.cn https://login.microsoftonline.com https://login.microsoftonline.us https://login.partner.microsoftonline.cn https://*.vault.azure.net https://*.vault.usgovcloudapi.net https://*.vault.azure.cn https://management.azure.com ..."

web-rs/Cargo.toml:51 (no Request/Response/fetch features, no gloo/reqwest):

.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:28:
- **CSP governs the *webview*, not backend egress.** `connect-src` in `tauri.conf.json` restricts only WASM frontend fetches; backend reqwest calls to new hosts need no CSP change.

The list is therefore dead permission that the repo's own rules say should not exist. It is not harmless: `https://*.vault.azure.net` lets any webview-side script bug exfiltrate data to an attacker-owned Key Vault hostname (Key Vault diagnostic logs record the request URI even for 401s), and the login/graph hosts give the same script a way to make authenticated-looking requests with the operator's browser cookies. Tauri appends its own IPC origins to connect-src at runtime, so `'self'` is sufficient.
proposal: Set `connect-src 'self'` in tauri.conf.json:25 (verify IPC + updater splash under `just dev`), add a repo_invariants test asserting connect-src contains no `https://` origin, and note in AGENTS.md / .claude/rules that the list is intentionally `'self'` only.
verifier_notes: Dead permission is real: tauri.conf.json:25 lists 13 remote origins; web-rs/Cargo.toml:51 enables no fetch/Request web-sys features and tauri-sys is used with `core`+`event` only (Cargo.toml:33), so the webview never contacts them. The repo's own rules say connect-src covers only frontend fetches (AGENTS.md:111, .claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:28, docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:56 'add the origin to the CSP only if the *frontend* fetches it'), so the list contradicts them. Overstated impact: sign-in happens in the system browser (loopback.rs `open_system_browser`), and the Tauri webview has its own cookie jar, so 'authenticated-looking requests with the operator's browser cookies' does not apply; and any script-execution bug in the webview already has IPC access to every backend command, which dwarfs a connect-src exfil path. Severity lowered to low (hygiene / defense in depth). Proposal to reduce to `'self'` is sound (Tauri appends its IPC origins automatically); the invariant test is simpler as an exact assertion that connect-src is `'self'` only.

title: Release-note markdown links render any `href` scheme, and the update splash feeds it the unsigned `latest.json` `notes` field
rationale: The minisign signature covers the downloaded bundle, not `latest.json`; its `notes` field is trusted only via TLS to github.com. Anyone who can edit the release asset (repo/CI compromise without the signing key) can therefore inject `[Update](javascript:...)` or a custom-scheme link that renders as a clickable anchor inside the privileged webview. Today `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` blocks `javascript:` navigation, so this is defense in depth rather than an exploitable hole — but it is the only remote-content-to-DOM path in the app and a one-line allowlist closes it independently of CSP.
proposal: In `parse_link` (or `render_inline`) accept only `https://` (optionally `http://`) hrefs and render anything else as plain text; add a unit test with `javascript:` and `file:` inputs next to the existing `parse_inline` tests. Mention in release-updater-demo.md that `notes` is unsigned content.
verifier_notes: changelog_notes.rs:376-383 accepts any href and :402 renders it as an anchor; update_splash.rs:82 feeds it `UpdateInfo.notes`, which updater.rs:32 fills from `update.body` (latest.json `notes`). The minisign signature covers the bundle, not latest.json, so `notes` is TLS-trusted content only; release-updater-demo.md:30-51 documents the notes contract without saying it is unsigned. Mitigations the reviewer already credits hold: `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` blocks `javascript:` navigation, and no opener/shell plugin is registered (lib.rs:24-25). release_notes.rs:52 also routes the build-time (trusted) notes through the same component, so an allowlist affects both harmlessly. Defense in depth; low is honest.

title: `?` opens the shortcuts sheet over an open modal, stacking two ModalShells with the same id and two focus traps; ten dialogs still hand-roll the ModalShell scaffold
rationale: With the update splash (or any ConfirmDialog) open, pressing `?` while focus is on a button opens the shortcuts sheet on top: two `id="modal-shell-title"` elements exist, both window-level Tab-cycling handlers are active, and one Escape closes both dialogs (every use_escape fires). Low frequency, but it is a real state the code allows. The ten hand-rolled dialogs also each hard-code a unique title id, which is why ModalShell's single fixed id was never questioned.
proposal: (1) In use_shortcuts skip bare-key bindings when `document.querySelector('.modal-backdrop')` exists (the workspace already uses this test — lift it into a `modal_is_open()` helper in hooks). (2) Give ModalShell a per-instance id (`format!("modal-title-{}", counter)`). (3) Migrate the 10 hand-rolled dialogs onto ModalShell (they are byte-identical outside their children), which also removes 10 copies of the hardcoded-id pattern and makes the FOCUSABLE fix below land once.

ShortcutsHelp, UpdateSplash and ReleaseNotesDialog are all ModalShells (shortcuts_help.rs:15, release_notes.rs, update_splash.rs) mounted together in shell.rs:524/532/533, and ModalShell hard-codes `id="modal-shell-title"` (modal_shell.rs:51-54) — ModalShell is also used in expose_api_tab, credentials_tab, dr.rs, app_roles and migrate_legacy_scope, so the duplicate-id exposure is wider than the finding says. use_escape.rs:18-24 is a plain window keydown listener with no topmost check, so every active dialog closes on one Escape, exactly as claimed; open_items_workspace.rs:26-33 already uses the `.modal-backdrop` query as a gate. Hand-rolled backdrops: 11 files / 12 renders (scope_wizard, add_owner, create_app, sso_wizard, scope_remediation ×2, gallery, new_app_chooser, confirm_dialog, cache_diagnostics, upload_certificate, secret_reveal), each with its own title id — the finding's "10" is one short. modal_shell.rs:7-8 acknowledges the predating dialogs but offers no rationale against migrating. Low is honest: rare, but a reachable state.

title: SecretRevealDialog reports 'Copied' even when the clipboard write fails, and a reflex Escape dismisses the one-time secret
rationale: `write_text` can reject (no focus, permission denied in some webviews); the dialog still flips to "Copied", and because `on_close` triggers `on_changed` the secret is gone for good once dismissed. Escape closes the reveal unconditionally, so an operator who habitually hits Esc after copying-that-failed loses the value. The credentials tab's `copy_pk` (972-982) gives no feedback at all, so a failed private-key copy is indistinguishable from success there.
proposal: Set `copied` only on `Ok(_)` and show a Callout on `Err` ("Couldn't copy — select the text and copy manually"); for both one-time reveals gate Escape (`use_escape(|| false, ...)`) or require the explicit Done button, and reuse `CopyIconButton`/`copy_text` so the feedback is the app-wide badge.
verifier_notes: secret_reveal_dialog.rs:21-28: `let _ = JsFuture::from(promise).await; copied.set(true);` flips the label regardless of rejection; :32 `use_escape(|| true, …)` closes on Escape unconditionally and `on_close` is what releases the deferred reload (credentials_tab.rs:390-397), so the value is gone. credentials_tab.rs:972-982 `copy_pk` discards the result with no feedback at all, and the gencert reveal has no `use_escape` (grep), so the two one-time reveals already behave differently. `CopyIconButton` (components/ui/copy_icon_button.rs) is the documented feedback primitive, though it too rides fire-and-forget `copy_text`, so honouring the promise result would need a small extension there.

title: SharePoint sites section (app-reg and enterprise panes) is gated on the bare `Sites.*` value instead of the resource-aware `is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission`
rationale: The row-level gate `row_scope_kind` (lines 70-81) and the `has_mail` gate three lines earlier (781-786, `is_exchange_scopable_on(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v)`) are resource-aware; this section gate is not. An app holding `Sites.Read.All` only on Office 365 SharePoint Online (or any third-party API exposing a `Sites.*` role) gets the `SharePointSitesSection`, which reads Graph per-site grants and will report "no grants" for a permission that section cannot describe. The repo invariant (`the_resource_blind_mailbox_gates_are_not_reintroduced`) only pins the Exchange forms, so nothing catches this.
proposal: Gate both call sites (permissions_tab.rs:808-814 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:253-258) on `is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v) || (v == "Sites.Selected" && resource is Graph or SPO)` — i.e. accept Graph + Office 365 SharePoint Online and reject other resources — or add a `is_sharepoint_site_grant_resource_permission` helper in core::scoping with that exact semantics and a unit test. Decide explicitly (doc comment on `SharePointSitesSection`, lines 7-11) whether SPO-resource apps keep the section; do not silently narrow to Graph-only. Optionally extend the repo invariant's GONE list to bare `is_sharepoint_orgwide(` calls outside core and scope_badge.

title: `LogAnalyticsClient::query` and the ARM list calls splice server-supplied ids (`customerId`, `subscriptionId`) into URL paths with no structural check, unlike `get_role_definition` which refuses the same class

Severity is low because the value follows a `/`, so the authority cannot change and the bearer stays on-origin; the exposure is path/query rewriting with the operator's own token.
proposal: Add `fn require_guid(s: &str) -> Result<()>` (36 chars, hex + hyphens) in `azapptoolkit-arm` and apply it to `workspace_customer_id`, every `subscription_id` parameter, and `principal_id` (currently only quote-escaped), returning `ArmError::Protocol`. Unit-test with `sub?api-version=x`, `../providers/…`, and a valid GUID.

By contrast `get_role_definition` (client.rs:133-151) refuses non-absolute ids, `?`/`#`, and off-origin authority, and its doc (:126-132) explicitly frames ARM response fields as attacker-influenced. The inconsistency with the crate's own stated threat model is real; practical exploitation requires attacker-controlled ARM responses and cannot move the bearer off-origin (value follows a `/`), so low is honest. `require_guid` for customerId/subscriptionId/principalId plus an absolute-path check for `scope` is small and consistent with existing guards.

title: Log Analytics `workspace_customer_id` from an ARM response is interpolated into the request path unvalidated, unlike the sibling `get_role_definition` guard

The ARM client's own doc comment classifies values echoed from ARM responses as attacker-influenced and validates them structurally before composing a URL; this second consumer of the same class has no check, so a value containing `/`, `?`, `#` or `..` reshapes the request (`?` would let a second query override `timespan`, `..` walks the path). Host is fixed, so impact is path/query reshaping, not SSRF — low is honest. `is_guid` lives only in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/guid.rs:37, unreachable from the arm crate, so the fix needs a small `core` helper (the proposal already allows this). title: Loopback honours an `error=` redirect before validating `state`, and writes the success page before the state check
rationale: RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 requires the error redirect to echo `state`, but the listener returns `Authorization(err)` on any request carrying `error=` without checking it. Any local process, or any web page open in the operator's browser (a cross-origin `fetch("http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?error=...")` still reaches the socket even though the response is opaque), can abort an in-flight sign-in and place an attacker-chosen string into the sign-in card (`"Sign-in failed: authorization request failed: {err}"`). The port is ephemeral but the range is small enough to spray. Separately, the browser tab is told "sign-in complete" even when `state` mismatches and the app is about to report `state_mismatch` — the page and the app disagree. `error_description` is also dropped, so the AADSTS code (65004 user-declined vs 53003 CA block) never reaches `aadsts_hint`.
proposal: Reorder: parse `state` first; if it is absent or mismatched, respond 400 with a neutral page and `continue` the accept loop (a forged request should not end the wait) rather than returning; only after `state` matches branch on `error`/`code`. Whitelist the surfaced `error` value (known OAuth codes) and carry `extract_aadsts_code(error_description)` into the message via `redacted_aad_error`-style formatting so the existing hint table fires. Extend `state_mismatch_is_rejected` to assert the forged request does not terminate the listener and that a later valid redirect still succeeds.
verifier_notes: Evidence real: loopback.rs:96-97 writes the 200 page, :99-101 returns `Authorization(err)` on any `error=` before the `state` check at :103-106, and `error_description` is never read (:65-72). The listener also ignores the HTTP method (:58 `let _method`), so even a CORS/PNA preflight `OPTIONS /?error=..` from a web page would terminate the wait. `state_mismatch_is_rejected` (:200-212) pins the current return-on-mismatch behaviour and would need updating as the proposal says. Message injection is text-only (Leptos renders text), so low is right; the proposal (validate `state` first, `continue` on forgery, carry the AADSTS code) is sound.

title: Loopback listener aborts the whole sign-in on a foreign `state` or `error` query from any local process, and serves the success page before validating
rationale: The listener already loops past favicon/preconnect noise, but a request carrying `?error=x` or `?code=x&state=forged` — which any unprivileged local process can send to the ephemeral port during the 300 s window — terminates the flow, so the real redirect that arrives moments later is lost and the operator sees 'state mismatch — possible CSRF' or the raw attacker-chosen `error` string in the toast. RFC 8252 loopback guidance is to ignore requests that do not match the outstanding state. The 200 'sign-in complete' page is also written before the state check, so a forged request gets a success page.
proposal: Validate `state == expected_state` before writing any response; on mismatch (or an `error` without a matching state) answer 400, log at warn, and `continue` the accept loop. Only after the state matches, branch on `error` vs `code` and write the success/failure page; constrain the surfaced `error` to `[a-z_]+`. Update `state_mismatch_is_rejected` to assert the genuine redirect is still delivered afterwards, and accept that a real mismatch now surfaces as the 300 s timeout.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: loopback.rs:86-99 writes the 200 'sign-in complete' page before any validation, then 100-106 returns on any `error` or mismatched `state`, so one forged request to the ephemeral port aborts the flow; dto/lib.rs:153-175 maps AuthError::Authorization via `err.to_string()`, so the attacker-chosen `error` text does reach the UI message. Existing test `state_mismatch_is_rejected` (loopback.rs:245-257) pins the current abort behaviour. Overstated: RFC 8252 discusses loopback interception risk but does not literally prescribe ignoring mismatched-state requests; the practical impact is a local DoS of one sign-in attempt by a process that knows the ephemeral port within the 300 s window. Trade-off the proposal omits: continuing the loop on mismatch means a genuine CSRF/mismatch now waits out the 300 s timeout instead of failing fast — acceptable, but it should be a deliberate choice with a warn! log.

title: InvalidGrant purge is unconditional, so a refresh still in flight across a completed reauthenticate can delete the new refresh token (narrow window)
rationale: Refresh locks are per `(tenant, scope_key)` by design, so two audiences refresh concurrently with the same RT. If refresh A (say ARM, on a slow link) is in flight when the session is re-established — `reauthenticate` or `consent_for_scopes` stores RT2 and re-inserts `known_tenants` — and A then returns `invalid_grant` for RT1, the arm deletes RT2 and removes the tenant: the operator who just completed a browser round trip is immediately "signed out" again and the reauth toast reappears. The window is a few seconds around every reauth, and the readiness fan-out (six concurrent refreshes) plus a 30 s HTTP timeout make it reachable. The purge should be conditional on the keyring still holding the token that failed.
proposal: Keep a monotonically increasing `session_generation: AtomicU64` bumped by `store_token_outcome`; capture it before `post_token` in `access_token_inner` and skip the purge (return `RefreshTokenMissing` without deleting/removing) when the generation changed — or compare the loaded RT to the stored one under `CHUNK_SET_LOCK` before deleting (`delete_refresh_token_if_eq`). Test: with a wiremock delay on one scope set, complete a `reauthenticate`-shaped store during the delay, then assert the keyring still holds RT2 and `known_tenants` is intact after the delayed `invalid_grant`.
verifier_notes: Logic verified: mod.rs:507-513 loads RT1 under the per-scope lock, :527-538 deletes whatever the keyring holds and removes the tenant on `InvalidGrant`, and `reauthenticate` (:661-673) stores RT2 and re-inserts the tenant with no generation check. But the rationale overstates reachability: for the race the failing `/token` POST must stay in flight for the entire browser round trip (seconds to tens of seconds) after the sibling refresh already purged and the operator completed reauth — realistic only with a badly stalled connection near the 30 s timeout, not 'a few seconds around every reauth'. The generation-counter fix is cheap and reasonable; low.

title: Blocking keyring delete runs inline on the tokio worker (and under the refresh lock), contradicting the crate's own rule
rationale: save_refresh_token (:457) and load_refresh_token (:509) are both wrapped in tokio::task::spawn_blocking with an explicit comment saying why, but delete_refresh_token is called synchronously twice: at :535 inside the refresh path while the refresh mutex is held (exactly the scenario the :503-506 comment warns about), and at :564 in sign_out. delete_chunks performs one OS keyring round trip per chunk (Windows Credential Manager; Linux secret-service over D-Bus via zbus), so an invalid-grant purge or a sign-out stalls the async worker and every other tokio task for the duration. The clippy `unused_async` hit on sign_out is the symptom that led here.
proposal: Wrap both calls the same way as save/load: `let (t, oid) = (tenant.tenant_id.clone(), tenant.account_oid.clone()); tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || delete_refresh_token(&t, &oid)).await.map_err(|e| AuthError::Keyring(format!("keyring delete task failed: {e}")))??;` at :564, and the `let _ =` form of the same at :535. Consider a private `async fn delete_refresh_token_blocking(&self, tenant)` helper so a third caller cannot regress. Effect: no tokio worker stall during sign-out or refresh-token purge; sign_out's `async` becomes genuine and the lint goes away.
verifier_notes: Evidence is real. crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:457 (save) and :509 (load) wrap the keyring call in tokio::task::spawn_blocking with the explicit rationale at :503-506 ('otherwise it stalls other tokio tasks while this holds the refresh lock'); :535 calls delete_refresh_token inline while the refresh mutex (:485-486) is still held, and :564 calls it inline in sign_out, which is a Tauri command (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs:49). token_cache.rs:376-396 shows delete_refresh_token -> delete_chunks does one keyring_core::Entry::delete_credential round trip per chunk. No comment, CHANGELOG entry, or docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md line justifies the asymmetry, and AuthError::Keyring(String) exists (auth/src/error.rs:45) so the proposed map_err shape compiles. Severity downgraded to low, not medium: both paths are rare (once per sign-out; once per InvalidGrant purge, where the keyring was just unlocked by the load at :509), Tauri's multi-thread runtime confines the stall to one worker rather than 'every other tokio task', and the lock held at :535 only delays refreshes for that same tenant/scope set which would wait anyway. Still a real consistency bug worth the small fix; the private helper suggestion is the right shape.

title: `TokenResponse` derives Debug with plaintext access, refresh and id tokens — the one secret-bearing type without a redacted Debug

The convention is real and repeatedly applied: hand-written redacting Debug on AccessToken (token_cache.rs:107-110), PasswordCredential (core/models.rs:273), SelfSignedCertificate (models.rs:940), SecretValue/SecretSetRequest (keyvault/models.rs:57/95), KvSecretValueDto/KvSetSecretInput (dto/keyvault.rs:72/106), RegeneratedSecret (dto/backup.rs:486), OidcSsoSummary (dto/sso.rs:252), GeneratedCertificateResult (dto/applications.rs:255), GeneratedCert (cert.rs:66), each with a `<redacted>` test. title: `Calendars.ReadWrite` keeps its PS-ported medium weight while the net-new `Contacts.ReadWrite` is high — reconcile or document the exception

The write=high sentence at 105-108 describes how the *net-new* additions were weighted. So this is a PS-parity vs net-new consistency question — a risk-model call, not a defect.

Rule 17 tells the operator to replace secrets with certificates; doing so with a normal certificate lifetime raises the app's score and files a misnamed finding. title: azure_roles: 'Log Analytics Reader' satisfaction set omits Reader/Contributor/Owner, so a Reader-only operator gets '?' instead of 'Have' despite the catalog saying '(or Reader)'
evidence:
azure_roles.rs:43:
        "Log Analytics Reader" => &[LOG_ANALYTICS_READER, LOG_ANALYTICS_CONTRIBUTOR],

capabilities.rs:365-368 (same capability's guidance):
        remediation: "Usage analysis needs Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings exporting \
                      MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs to a Log Analytics workspace, the Log Analytics \
                      Reader Azure RBAC role (or Reader) on that workspace, plus the \
                      api.loganalytics.azure.com scope.",
